Having placed [the thread] upon the breast in the presence of Śiva, he should tie it as before. Afterwards, visualizing the Pāśasūtra together with the iḍā and piṅgalā [nāḍīs] as the lotus-stalk through the suṣumnā nāḍī, [he recites]: "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Suṣumnā."

Having thus remained within the body of Śiva, having taken up the Suṣumṇā-nāḍī, joined it with the thread, and performed worship and the avaguṇṭhana, he offers three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the disciple’s proximity. Then, having purified the prārabdha-deha which serves as the basis for all the disciple’s karma of enjoyment, and because the power of enjoyment exists therein, [the Guru] places [the deity] in the maṇḍala-sthāna upon the head of the disciple.

Having worshipped Śakti with "Oṃ hauṃ śaktaye namaḥ," having taken it from the head, having placed it upon the thread (sūtra), having worshipped it, and having performed the encircling (avaguṇṭhana), one should perform the invocation (sannidhāna). Having offered three oblations (āhutis) with the root mantra, one should sprinkle the disciple's heart with the Astra mantra, [reciting] "Oṃ haḥ."

Having performed the *tāḍana* with flowers while uttering "Hūṃ Phaṭ," and while emitting the sound "Huṃ," he [the preceptor] should emerge through his own *rāśaka-nāḍī* and enter the disciple's heart through the disciple's *bhrū-raṅga* by way of the *vāma-nāḍī*. Then, meditating on the *haṃsa-bīja* as a shining, star-like form that abides illuminating the consciousness (*caitanya*) of the disciple, he should awaken that consciousness by reciting "Oṃ Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ. [Then] "Oṃ Hāṃ Haṃ..."

Saying "HĀṂ SVĀHĀ," having taken [the breath] by means of the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, one should lead it up to the limit of the *dvādaśānta* (the twelve-finger space above the head). Having taken it through the *nāḍī* of the recipient's *reca* (exhalation) breath, one causes it to enter one's own heart by means of the *pūraka* (inhalation) breath. Then, by means of the *kumbhaka* (retention) breath, one brings about a state of oneness (*ekībhāva*) within the *śivasthāna* (abode of Śiva) at the heart. Having led it back again to the limit of one's own *dvādaśānta*, one returns once more by way of the *sr̥ṣṭikrama* (process of emanation) to the limit of the *brūmadhya* (the middle of the brows).

Through the southern channel by means of one's own *rāśaka* power, [one should recite]: "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ ātmane namaḥ," join it to the thread, and perform the *avaguṇṭhana*. Then, for the purpose of bringing [the deity] into presence (*sannidhāna*), offer three oblations with the root mantra. Afterwards, [recite]: "Oṃ hāṃ bhoktṛtvakāraṇāya malaprakṣālanāya namaḥ" [to the one] of black complexion; and "Oṃ hāṃ laukikādikarmaprakṣālebhyaḥ sukṛtaduṣkṛtabhogakāraṇebhyo namaḥ."
Thus, as white and non-white forms: *oṃ hāṃ māyāpāśāya śaśirendriyaviṣayakāraṇāya namaḥ*; and as various colors: *oṃ hāṃ pāśādhiṣṭhātṛyai śivaśaktaye namaḥ*.

Having thus meditated upon that as being of the nature of darkness (*tamaḥ-svarūpa*), having extracted [the bonds] from the body of the disciple and joined them to the *pāśasūtra*, and having worshipped them, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of their presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, having meditated upon the bonds—beginning from the *śāntyatītanāda*—as the instruments (*kārakāḥ*) across the fourteen paths (*adhvans*) such as the *tattvas* and *bhuvanas*, and having extracted them from the body of the disciple, [one places them] in the location of the *pāśasūtra*...

Having joined [the mantra] therein with "Oṃ Hauṃ Śāntyatītakalāyai Namaḥ," one should perform the act of inspection (*nirīkṣaṇa*). Then, in accordance with the method of joining the *tattvas* and *bhuvanas*, one should join the *tattvas*: the *Śivatattva* and the *Śaktitattva*; and the *bhuvanas*: Anāśratā, Anantā, Anādā, Vyomarūpā, and Vyāpinī. Thus, there are five—the *Śakti*, *Śiva*, *Kalā*, and *Bhuvana*s—within the *Śivatattva*. Furthermore, within the *Śivatattva* are: 1. Ūrdhvakāminī, 2. Rociṇī, 3. Moṣiṇī, 4. [Tā?]pikā, 5. [Name missing].

The worlds known as Idikai, which cause even the trembling sky and the Śaktitattva to tremble, exist together with the enjoyments of the Tūryasama state. Furthermore, there are the sixteen phonemes—A, Ā, I, Ī, U, Ū, Ṛ, Ṝ, Ḷ, Ḹ, E, AI, O, AU, Aṃ, and Aḥ—as well as the word "Oṃ," and the mantras: "Oṃ Hāṃ Hauṃ Śivāya Namaḥ," "Oṃ Hoṃ Īśānamūrtaye Namaḥ," and "Oṃ Haḥ Astrāya Namaḥ."

(1.4) The mantras beginning with *yenakim*; the egg (*aṇḍa*) consisting of the seed-syllable (*bīja*), the resonance (*nāda*), the syllable *oṃ*, and the syllable *hauṃ*; the two senses beginning with *nādī* and *huṃ śaṅkinī*; (1.5) the two vital airs (*vāyu*) beginning with *devatattva* and *tattvajñayana*; the two senses beginning with *vacana* and *śrotra*; a single object which is sound (*śabda*); the quality of sound (*śabdaguṇa*); the white-colored sphere of *vṛttākāra-maṇḍala*; and the state beyond the *duryādīta*.

Having meditated upon the Śāntyatīta-kalā as being present within the Lord who is the Cause, Sadāśiva, one should perform the touching with flowers on the head while reciting "Oṃ hāṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ. Then, inhaling through the pūraka breath with the saṃhāra-mudrā, one should recite: "Oṃ hauṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ."

Having joined [the thread] to the head according to the *sūtra*, purified it, and performed the *avaguṇṭhana* (veiling), one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) with this mantra for the sake of its presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, one should perform the gazing (*nirīkṣaṇa*) with the mantra: *oṃ hyai śāntikalāyai namaḥ*. The principles of Īśvara—Sūkṣma, Śivottama, Ekanetra, Oṃkāra, Raudra, Trimūrti, Śrīkaṇṭha, and Śikhaṇḍin—and the seven worlds; the nineteen worlds of Śuddhavidyā—Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikaraṇī, Balavikaraṇī, Balapramathanī, Sarvabhūtadamani, and Manonmanī; and the three phonemes Ka, Kha, and Ga, which are the lords of these worlds: 1. Vyonavyāpine, 2. Vyomarūpāya, 3. [3. ... (Note: The text fragment provided ends with "3. and does not contain the full third name.)

To the all-pervading (1), to Śiva (2), to the infinite (3), to the beginningless (4), to the unsupported (5), to the eternal (6), to the everlasting (7), to him who is established on the seat of Yoga (8), to the perpetual yogi (9)—with these eleven words, one for each [deity], [one should worship]. [One should meditate upon] the two mantras *oṃ haim kavacāya vaṣaṭ* and *ye na*, as well as the two seeds *bindu* and *yāga-mūma*, the two nāḍīs *alampuruṣai* and *yaśai*, the two faces *kūrman* and *krukarana*, the two organs *tvak* and *pādam*, the object *sparśa*, and the qualities *śabda* and *sparśa*, as well as the state of *duryāva*, [all] within a hexagon.

Meditating upon the peaceful art (śāntikalā) as a black-colored maṇḍala that pierces through Īśvara and Maheśvara, [one should say]: "Oṃ hraiṃ śāntikalāyai huṃ phaṭ. Having struck the forehead with the fist and performed the striking with flowers at the location from the root to the end of the nose, one should inhale with the *pūraka* breath using the *saṃhāramudrā*, [saying]: "Oṃ hraiṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ."

Having joined [the mantra] thus according to the *Mukhasūtra*, having worshipped [it], and having performed the *avaguṇṭhana* (veiling), one who offers three oblations (*āhuti*) with this mantra ending in *svāhā* for the purpose of [ensuring] the presence [of the deity]: *Oṃ hūṃ vidyālayāya namaḥ*—thus performing the *nirīkṣaṇa* (gazing). [One should contemplate] the seven *kalās*: Māyā, Kāla, Niyati, Kalā, Vidhyā, Rāga, and Puruṣa; and the eight *tattvas*: Īśāna, Ekeṣaṇa, Ekapiṅgala, Utpava, Bhava, Vāmadeva, Mahāteja, and Yena. 1. Mahādyuti. 2. [The second].

Having joined [the mantra] thus in the Sūtra, having worshipped, and having performed the avaguṇḍana, this becomes the presence (*sannidhāna*). These two mantras [pervade] the two vital breaths known as udāna and samāna, the two faculties known as vāyu-jihvā, the object of taste, and the four qualities of sound, touch, form, and taste. They reside within the white, half-moon-shaped maṇḍala, the state of dreaming, and as the causal Lord Viṣṇu.

Having performed the meditation on the *pratiṣṭhākalā* with "Oṃ hvlīṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai huṃ phaṭ," he strikes the disciple's navel and the two knees with the *vākpuṣpa* flower. Then, for the purpose of invoking the presence (*sannidhāna*), while offering three oblations (*āhutis*) with the *yirukura-mantra*, he subsequently performs the rite of gazing (*nirīkṣaṇa*) with "Oṃ hlāṃ navṛttikalāyai namaḥ."

Above the single *pṛthvī-tattva* (earth element), there are the worlds known as Bhadrakālī and Vīrabhadra. Above the *brahmāṇḍa*, there are ten worlds: Trilocana, Nabholipsu, Vivāhana, Samvāhana, Triśeśvara, Tryakṣa, Kaṇādhyakṣa, Vibhu, Śambhu, and [the world of] Bhadrakālī and Vīrabhadra. Below these worlds, above the *brahmāṇḍa*, there are ten worlds: 1. Candra, 2. Daṃṣṭrin, 3. ... [and so on].

The ten worlds of Brahmāṇḍa are: 1. Phaṇīndra, 2. Audumbarīśa, 3. Grasana, 4. Mārutāśana, 5. Krodhana, 6. Ananta, 7. Vṛṣadhara, 8. Vṛṣan, 9. Balipriya, 10. Trapāla. The ten worlds of Īśāna are: 1. Jyeṣṭha, 2. Śarva, 3. Sureśāna, 4. Vedapāraga, 5. Jñānabhuk, 6. Sarvajña, 7. Īśa, 8. Vidyādhipa, 9. Prakāmada, 10. [The tenth is implied].

In the north, there are ten worlds: 1. Prasādaka, 2. Śrīdhara, 3. Ratnadhara, 4. Lakṣmīdhara, 5. Jaṭādhara, 6. Saumyadeha, 7. Dhanya, 8. Rūpavān, 9. Nidhīśa. In the north, there are ten worlds: 1. Meghavāhana, 2. Kapartin, 3. Pañcaśikha, 4. Pañcāntaka, 5. Kṣayāntaka, 6. Tīkṣṇa, 7. Sūkṣma, 8. Vāyuvega, 9. Vapuśīghra. (Note: Only nine are listed. 1. [The tenth is missing.]

In the southwest corner (Nirṛti), there are ten worlds: 1. Daṃṣṭravān, 2. Lohita, 3. Dhūmra, 4. Virūpākṣa, 5. Ūrdhvaretas, 6. Bhayānaka, 7. Krūradaṃṣṭrin, 8. Hantṛ, 9. Māraṇa, 10. Nirṛti. In the southern direction, there are [seven] worlds: 1. Adharmapati, 2. Viyoktṛ, 3. Saṃyoktṛ, 4. Vidhātṛ, 5. Dhātṛ, 6. Haramṛtyu, 7. Yāmya. [Furthermore: 1. Kṣayāntaka, 2. Bhasmāntaka, 3. ... [in the southern direction].

Babhru (4), Dahanana (5), Jvalana (6), Harana (7), Ghatana (8), Pingalana (9), and Hutashana (10)—these are the ten worlds belonging to Agni-Rudra. Tridashadhipa (1), Pinaki (2), Shasta (3), Avyadha (4), Vibhuti (5), Parardana (6), Vajradehana (7), Buddhana (8), Ajana (9), and Kapalishana (10)—these are the ten worlds belonging to the eastern direction. Rudrana (1), Vishnu (2), Brahma (3), and Hatakan (4)... [The text continues with further names].

Kūṣmāṇḍas 6. Kālāgni: In the center of the Brahmāṇḍa, there are the worlds (bhuvanās). Having pierced through the worlds of the great ones equal to Rudra, [one reaches] the hundred worlds and the phoneme *kṣa*. O Mahādevasadbhāveśvara, O Lord of Great Splendor and Master of Yoga, release, release! First, first! All, all! Be, be! O Source of Existence, O Bestower of Happiness upon all beings!

O you who cause all to be present; O Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra; O supreme one; O you who are worshipped by those not yet worshipped; O you who are praised by those not yet praised; O witness of what was previously situated and what is currently situated; bear witness! O Kuru; O Pataṅga; O Piṅga like a sun-bird; O Piṅga of knowledge; O Śabda of knowledge; O Śabda that is subtle; O Sūkṣma-Śiva; O bestower of all things, O Sarvada; Oṃ, salutations, salutations! Oṃ. [These are] the twenty-eight words. Oṃ Haṃ, salutations to the form of Sadyojāta; Oṃ Hāṃ, salutations to the Heart. [These are] the two mantras.

Meditation on the cessation [of the elements] consists of visualizing the seed-syllables *a* and *ka*, the channels known as *iḍā* and *piṅgalā*, the vital airs known as *apāna* and *prāṇa*, the organs known as the *upastha* and the *ghrāṇa* (nose), the object of smell (*gandha*), and the five qualities (*pañcaguṇa*)—sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—as yellow, situated within the square mandala of the earth element, corresponding to the waking state (*jāgaravasthā*), and presided over by Brahmā, who bears the name Kāraṇeśvara. This is the meditation on cessation (*nivartikā dhyāna*).

Having performed [the preliminary rites], one should inhale with the *pūraka* breath using the *saṃhāramudrā*, reciting "oṃ hlāṃ nivartikalāyai namaḥ," and having joined [the deity] to the *pāda-sūtra* and worshipped it, one should perform the *avaguṇṭhana*. Then, offering three oblations (*āhutitraya*) with the mantra ending in *svāhā*—this mantra consisting of [the sequence]: the mantras together with their *padas*, the *padas* together with their *varṇas*, the *varṇas* together with their *bhuvanas*, the *bhuvanas* together with their *tattvas*, and the *tattvas* as the *kalās*.

Tattva, Bhuvana, Varṇa, Pada, and Mantra are the objects of pervasion. Furthermore, Mala, Karma, and Māyā are pervasive within these [categories], and conversely, the Śāntyātītā and other Kalās are pervasive within Mala and the others. Having thus contemplated this, one should offer [the oblation] to each [category] individually by means of the Śāntyātīta-kalā-mantras, ending with *svāhā*. Then, [one should recite]: *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hūṃ śāntyātītakalāyai huṃ phaṭ*.
Oṃ hūṃ haiṃ hūṃ śāntikalāyai hūṃ phaṭ. (1.5) Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ vidyākalāyai hūṃ phaṭ. Oṃ hūṃ hvīṃ hūṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai hūṃ phaṭ.

Oṃ hūṃ hlāṃ hūṃ nivṛttikalāyai hūṃ phaṭ. Having thus offered three oblations for each as illumination, one should worship Śiva along with His limbs in the locations of the *sūtra-kalās*—namely the *brahmarandhra*, *bhrūmadhya*, *kaṇṭha*, *nābhi*, and *jānu*—using substances such as saffron and others applied according to the ritual procedure; then [recite] Oṃ haḥ...

Saying "Hūṃ Phaṭ," he performs the striking (*tāḍana*) on the head of the disciple with the *nārāca-mudrā* using a flower-stalk from the thread, and [recites]: "Oṃ Hraum! Salutation to the Śāntyatīta-kalā."

Having entered within [the thread] and drawn it out, one should join it to the *sūtra* with this mantra, performing three oblations ending in *svāhā*: *oṃ hauṃ hauṃ hauṃ bhagavan śāntyatītakalāpāśamalakarmanāyakaśaktitattvabhuvanādibyāpakam bandha bandha huṃ phaṭ*. Having thus finished with the *sūtra*, afterwards, at the location of the forehead-thread (*lalāṭasūtrapradeśe*), [one should utter]: *oṃ haḥ*.

Having performed the touching (*tāḍana*) with the *puṣpatīnāla* while reciting *Hūṃ Phaṭ*, one enters and takes [the thread], joins it to the *sūtra*, and offers three oblations (*āhuti*) ending in *svāhā* with this mantra: *Oṃ Saim Śāntikalāyai Namaḥ*. Then, while tying the knot in the *sūtra* with the mantra *Oṃ Hauṃ Hryaiṃ Hauṃ Bhagavan Śāntikalāpāśamalakarmanāyāśaktitattvabhuvanādivyāpakam Bandha Bandha Hūṃ Phaṭ Ye*, one subsequently [recites] *Oṃ Haḥ* over the *kalaśa-sūtra*.

Having performed the *tāḍana* with flowers while reciting *hūṃ phaṭ ye*, and having entered [the thread] by taking it up with *oṃ hrūṃ vidyākalāyai namaḥ*, one joins it to the *sūtra*. Then, offering three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with *svāhā* using this mantra, one ties the knot in the *sūtra* while reciting: *oṃ hauṃ hrūṃ hauṃ bhagavan vidyākalāpāśamalakarmanāyāpāśaśaktitattvabhuvanādivyāpakam bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ ye*.

Afterwards, having performed the *tāḍana* with flowers upon the navel-thread (*nābhisūtra*) while reciting *oṃ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ ye*, and having entered [the deity] while reciting *oṃ hvīṃ pratiṣṭhākālāyai namaḥ*, one should join it to the thread. Then, having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) ending in *svāhā* with this mantra, one should [bind] it to the thread while reciting: *oṃ hauṃ hvīṃ hauṃ bhagavan pratiṣṭhākālāpāśamalakarmaniyāśaktitattvabhuvanādivyāpakam bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ ye*.

Having tied a knot at the end [of the thread], one should perform the *tāḍana* upon the thread with a flower-stalk while reciting "Oṃ Haḥ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā. Then, having entered [the thread] while reciting "Oṃ Hlāṃ Nivṛttikalāyai Namaḥ," one should take [the deity] out and join it to the thread. With this mantra ending in *svāhā*, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*). Finally, one should tie a knot at the end of the thread while reciting: "Oṃ Hauṃ Hlāṃ Hauṃ Bhagavan, bind, bind the bonds of the Nivṛttikalā-pāśa, mala, karma, and Māyā, which pervade the pure principles (*śuddhatattva*), worlds (*bhuvana*), and so forth; Hūṃ Phaṭ!"

Thereafter, having placed that thread upon his right shoulder, he should offer one hundred oblations with the *mūla-mantra* for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*). Having taken up that thread and placed it in a vessel, he should consecrate it with the *hṛdaya-mantra* and the *astra-mantra*, worship it with only those [mantras], and perform a *saṃbhāra-homa* with the *saṃhitā-mantra*. Then, having informed the Lord of the Maṇḍala, he should place it in the "Śiva-tree" at the breast of the pitcher, saying: "This..."

Having made this petition, "Please grant me protection," he should thereafter perform obeisance preceded by worship to the *iṣṭaliṅga*, Śivakumbha, Sthāṇumaṇḍaleśvara, Agnisthāṇu, and others, along with their respective mantras and the disciple. Then, having entered the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*), he should draw three maṇḍalas; placing the disciple in the eastern direction facing west and in the northern direction facing south within the first maṇḍala, he should place darbha grass in his hand and [recite] three times.

The Śulaktriyas, having been made to perform ācamana with the *pañcagavya* at the center by the Ātmatattvādis, partook of it. Standing in the second maṇḍala (l. 8), they partook of the sacrificial rice (*caru*)—which had not stuck to the ladle in three places, nor to the eight places, nor to the handle—with the five limbs (*pañcāṅgulayaḥ*), together with the ācamanas at the center. Standing in the third maṇḍala (l. 9), they offered the tooth-stick (*dantakāṣṭha*) with the heart-mantra, performed the purification of the teeth (*dantaśuddhi*), and [offered] the tooth-stick.

Having bound [the disciple], made him ascend, and caused him to prostrate, he then placed the *dantakāṣṭha* (tooth-stick). Having determined the directions—east, north, northeast, and west—if it falls in these directions, it is auspicious; if it falls in other directions, it is inauspicious. Having understood this, he causes him to perform *ācamana* and enters within. For the purpose of pacifying any defects regarding the placement of the *dantakāṣṭha*, he performs one hundred and eight oblations (*homa*) with the *astra-mantra*, for the sake of the disciple...

For the purpose of pacifying the defects arising from the mind, speech, and body, one should perform oblations separately with the *mūla-mantra* and the *aghorāstra-mantra*, each repeated one hundred times. Subsequently, for the sake of the monthly *tarpaṇa*, one should perform homa as much as possible with the *caru*, sesame seeds, clarified butter (*ājya*), and other materials, using the *mūla-mantra* along with the five Brahma-mantras and the six ancillaries (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Having performed the *pūrṇāhuti*, one should offer three oblations ending with "svāhā" using the *mūla-mantra* for the purpose of the *naivedya* from the remnants of the *caru*. This concludes with the rites beginning from the sipping of water (*ācamana*) up to the recitation (*japa*).

Having worshipped and made this petition: "O Lord of the Two, from the *ādhārakarma* onwards, Your presence must not be offered here for the destruction of the fetters of bound souls (*paśu*s)," he obstructs Śiva at the station of the fire. Having performed the *homa* with the *pūrādimantras*, he consecrates the fire as the *mūrti*. He offers oblations to Brahmā and others, as well as to Indra and others, and then dismisses them. He offers internal oblations (*antarbali*) to Rudra and others, and external oblations (*bahirbali*) to Indra and others, and then dismisses them.

In the mandala [resembling] a lotus (maṇḍalopola), having formed the head [of the deity] as the Lord of the Mandala (maṇḍaleśvara) and the Lord of the Vessel (kumbheśvara) for the sake of the weapon’s expansion (astravartanikā), he spoke of the sacrificial deities (yāgadevatās) together with the *parāṅmukhārghya*. Having spoken in reverse and having awakened [the deity], he performed the worship of Caṇḍeśvara. Afterwards, in the sacrificial pavilion (yāgamaṇḍapa), having consecrated the darbha-bed (darbhaśayana) one hundred times with the Astra-mantra, he placed the Navanatha of Bhokeśvara with the head toward the east; and the Navanatha of Mokṣeśvara upon the bed of pure ashes (śuddhabhasmaśayana) with the head toward the north and the feet toward the south.
Having made them ascend the bed with the Hṛdaya-mantra...
He holds a khaṭvāṅga, the supreme mudrā, a trident, and likewise the gesture of fearlessness;
he is a dream-child, tawny in hue, with matted hair and the crescent moon as his crest-ornament.

Having meditated in this manner, [one should recite]: *Oṃ namaśśambho triṇetrāya mahātmane | vāmāya viśvarūpāya svapnādhipataye namaḥ || Ācakṣva devadeveśa prapanno'smi tavāntike | svapne kāryāṇi sarvāṇi hṛdisthāni nibodha me ||* "Obeisance to Śambhu, the three-eyed one, the Great Soul; obeisance to the Auspicious One, whose form is the universe, the Lord of Dreams. Speak, O Lord of the Gods, for I have sought refuge at your side. Reveal to me all the matters concerning my dreams that reside within my heart."

Having thus made this petition, and having instructed the disciple with the mantra "Oṃ him him hili hili śūlapāṇaye svāhā," he causes him to sleep and covers him with new garments consecrated by the kavaca-mantras.

Afterwards, having drawn three lines with rice, mustard seeds, and ashes, and having consumed the *pañcagavya* and the sacrificial oblation (*caru*), he performs the purification of the teeth (*dantaśuddhi*). Following this, after performing the bath with ashes (*bhasmasnāna*) preceded by sipping water (*ācamana*), he goes to sleep. If it is his first night [in the vow], he does not perform the rites beginning with the *tapaḥ* (austerity) mentioned hereafter, such as the binding of the *pāśasūtra*.

Since the two hundred and twenty-four worlds previously mentioned do not exist even among the perishable and imperishable [realms], and since the three paths have been excluded, I shall state the names of the *tattva*-worlds and their presiding deities. The ritual of consecration (*adhivāsanavidhi*) is completed.

On the day of Madanāha, having risen early with the morning breeze and performed his bath—both the daily (*nitya*) and the occasional (*naimittika*) rites—and having completed the *saṃdhyā* and other rituals as prescribed, he then summoned his disciple. Having heard the disciple's dream, if there were inauspicious dreams, he performed a *homa* for the purpose of pacification (*śānti*).

Having heard [the following], one should act accordingly: eating curd, fish, meat, and liquor; wearing white garments; placing eggs upon oneself; seeing these things in a dream is auspicious. Applying oil to one's own limbs; anointing the body with sesame oil; falling into a swamp; wearing a garland of *śivandapida* flowers; and knowing oneself to be devoid of splendor—[these are inauspicious].

Regarding the expiation for bad dreams, he says: one who performs a thousand *mūrdhā-homas* with the Astra-mantra; or, if performing two thousand *mūrdhā-homas*, then, after entering within the maṇḍapa and performing the daily rites (*nityakarman*) up to the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*), having performed the *kalānyāsa* and placing the hand of Śiva upon himself, having worshipped Śiva in the "breast" of the pitcher (*kumbha-stana*), and having honored Indra and the others preceded by meditation, [he worships] the Lord of the Maṇḍala and the one in the "breast" of the fire (*vahnistana*).

Having worshipped these [deities], one should perform a hundred oblations for each of the hundred forms with the root mantra ending in *svāhā* as the general and specific *darbha*-offerings (*tarpaṇa*), and ten-tenths (*daśāṃśa*) for the limbs of Brahmā (*brahmāṅga*). After performing the *pūrṇāhuti*, one should perform an oblation for the pacification of bad dreams. Then, having performed the *tarpaṇa* and *dīpana* for the root mantra and the other mantras, one should proceed—either by means of the rites beginning with the entry of the disciple (*śiṣyapraveśa*) and ending with the *nāḍīsaṃtāna* and the *sambhāra-homa*, or according to the method prescribed for initiation—and having reached the station of the fire (*vahnisthāna*), [one should conclude].

Having petitioned, "Grant grace to Paśu, who is under the protection of Kumbheśvara," he brought the Pāśasūtra, performed the *aṅganyāsa* upon the disciple, worshipped him with the *Saṃhitās*, and, as before, gave him the book according to the instruction of compassion (*avanutaya-śikṣā*).

Having petitioned Yageśvara, saying, "I shall bestow grace upon Paśu," and having caused the initiation to be performed, one should meditate upon the aforementioned *kalās*—which have been purified within oneself, within the fire-pit (*agni-sthāna*), within the maṇḍaleśvara-pitcher, within the kumbheśvara-pitcher, and within the disciple—as being pervaded and pervasive along with the mantra-words, syllables, and worlds. Then, for the purpose of uniting them one by one, one should offer one hundred oblations (*āhuti*) with the root-mantra.

Having performed the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), thereafter, having worshipped within the fire with "oṃ hām ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ," one should offer three oblations ending in *svāhā* using that mantra for the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity (*sannidhāna*). Then, meditating on its pervasion at the station of the Nivṛtti-kalā below the knee upon the disciple's sacred thread (*pāśasūtra*) with "oṃ hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai namaḥ" and "oṃ hāṃ pṛthvītatvāya namaḥ."
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kālāgnirudra; to Kūśmāṇḍa, Hāṭaka, Brahmā, Vaiṣṇava, Rudra, Kapālīśa, Aja, Buddha, Vajradeha, Pramardana, Vibhūti, and Hāsya; to the Teacher, Pinākin.

To the Lord of the Thirty-three, Agni, Rudra, Hutāśana, Piṅgala, Ghātaka, Hara, Jvalana, Dahana, Babhru, Bhasmāntaka, Kṣayāntaka, Yāmya, Mṛtyuhara, Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Kartṛ, Saṃyoktṛ, Viyoktṛ, Dharmapati, Adharmapati, Nirṛti, Māraṇa, Hantr, Krūradaṃṣṭrin, Bhayānaka, Ūrdhvaretas, Virūpākṣa, Dhūmra, Lohitadaṃṣṭrin, Bala, Atibala, Pāśahasta, Mahā...
Śvetabalabhadra, Dīrghabāhu, Jalāntaka, Meghanāda, Sunāda, Śīghra, Laghu, Vāyuvega, Sūkṣma, Tīkṣṇa, Kṣayāntaka, Pañcāntaka, Pañcaśikha, Kapardin—

To Meghavāhana... to Rūpavān, Dhanya, Saumyadeha, Jaṭādhara, Lakṣmīdhara, Ratnadhara, Prasādaka, Prakāmada, Vidyādhipa, Īśa, Sarvajña, Jñānabhuk, Vedapāraka, Sureśa, Śarva, Jyeṣṭha, Bhūtapāla, Balipriya, Vṛṣa, Vṛṣadhara, Ananta, Krodhana, Mārutāśana, Gṛdhanā, Udumbarīśa, Phaṇīndra, Vajradaṃṣṭrin, Śambhu, Vibhu, Gaṇādhyakṣa, Tridaśeśvara, Saṃvāha, Vivāha, and Nabha.
—Salutations to Lipsā, Trilocana, Vīrabhadra, Bhadrakālī, and the worlds. Also: *Oṃ hāṃ kṣakārāya namaḥ*. Also: *Oṃ hāṃ oṃ namo namaḥ oṃ śivāya oṃ namo namaḥ*.

Salutation to the Lord of Yoga, who is Sarvada, Śarva, Śiva, Sūkṣma, Sūkṣma-śabda, Śabda-jñāna, Jñāna-piṅga, Piṅga-pataṅga, Pataṅga-kuru, Kuru-sākṣi, Sākṣi-pūrvasthita, Pūrvasthita-anarcita, Anarcita-brahmaviṣṇurudrapara, Sarvasānnidhyapara, Sarvabhūtasukhaprada, Bhavodbhava, Bhava, Śarva, Śarva-prathama, Prathama-muñca, Muñca. *Note: The sequence of names follows the specific order and phonetic structure of the original Sanskrit verse.*

Salutations to Mahātejas, Sadbhāva, Īśvara, and Mahādeva. Also: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Heart*; (l. 7) *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Sadyojāta form*; also *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the seed-syllables A and La*; also *Oṃ hām, salutation to the channels Iḍā and Piṅgalā*; also *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the vital winds Prāṇa and Apāna*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the sense organs of smell and generation*; *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the objects of smell*.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the qualities of smell, taste, form, touch, and sound. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Brahmakāraṇeśvara. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the waking state.

Having worshipped [it] thus for the sake of prosperity, and having visualized the earth-maṇḍala as a four-cornered vajra, you remain absorbed in meditation upon the Nivṛtti-kalā, which remains encompassing within itself the fourteen types of births—beasts, birds, domestic animals, reptiles, stationary beings, humans, piśācas, rākṣasas, yakṣas, gandharvas, Indra, Soma, Prajeśvara, Brahmā, and Māna. Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ nivṛttikalāyai huṃ.

Saying "phaṭ," strike with a flower-stalk below the knees. Then, saying "oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai svāhā," inhale there with the *pūraka* breath and the *śaṅkha-mudrā*. Next, saying "oṃ hauṃ hlāṃ hauṃ nivṛttikalāyai huṃ phaṭ," take it up along with the *kuṇḍa* using the *saṃhāra-mudrā*. Finally, saying "oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ nivṛttikalāyai namaḥ," exhale (*recaka*) and, using the *udbhava-mudrā*, [place it] in the *kuṇḍa* within the *ādhāra-śakti*.

Having placed [the deity] with "Oṃ hāṃ hlāṃ hāṃ niva(vṛ)ttikalāyai namaḥ," having worshipped and offered the arghya, one should offer three oblations ending in svāhā with this mantra. Then, for the purpose of bringing about the presence (sannidhāna), having meditated upon the three powers—mala, karma, and māyā—as well as the state of being the enjoyer (bhoktṛtva) and the body which is the instrument of enjoyment (bhogāṅgaśarīra), one should subsequently invoke Brahmā with "Oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ," worship him, and offer three oblations ending in svāhā with that same mantra.

Having offered three oblations with the *sannidhālā* mantra: "In this office of Brahmā, I initiate this seeker of liberation; you must act as Anusūla by the command of the Supreme Lord. The meaning of this is: "I shall initiate the disciple who desires liberation within your office as Brahmā."

Having petitioned Śivāñjali, saying, "May you be favorable," one should then form the mental resolve (*saṅkalpa*) regarding the wombs (*yoni*) beginning with the stationary (*sthāvara*), which exist within this *kalā*. One should meditate upon Vāgīśvarī as pervading those [wombs] with the mantra: *oṃ hāṃ vāgīśvaryai namaḥ*.

Having performed the invocation (*āvāhana*) thus, having worshipped, and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with *svāhā* for the purpose of establishing presence (*sannidhāna*), one should meditate upon Vāgīśvara as five-faced and four-armed. Then, saying *oṃ hāṃ vāgīśvarāya namaḥ*, and recollecting him as the one who causes the agitation of all wombs (*sarvayonikṣobhakara*) and the destroyer of obstacles (*nirūpaka*), one should perform the invocation and worship. Having offered three oblations ending with *svāhā* at this point for the sake of establishing presence, [one should pray: "For the sake of showing grace (*anugraha*) toward me, may you remain present."

Having prayed, "Please do so," he should sprinkle the disciple with the Astra-mantra. Then, saying "Oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ," he should strike the disciple's heart with flowers. Accompanied by the syllable *Huṃ*, he should enter the body of the disciple through his own *rēcaka* breath. Then, saying "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ," and again "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā," he should take [the disciple] up with the *śaṅkha-mudrā*. Having recited the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), [he should perform the rite for] him...

Having led [the soul] to the dvādaśānta, one should meditate upon the individual soul (ātman), which is like a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, and by means of the saṃhāramudrā, withdraw it with the mantra *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ ātmane namaḥ* (l. 8). Then, placing it within one’s own heart along with the inhaled breath (pūraka-vāyu), one should retain it (kumbhita) and recite the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*). Finally, with the mantra *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ ātmane namaḥ* (l. 9), [one should worship] Brahmā and the other deities...

Having gradually led [the deity] up to his own Dvādaśānta and then brought it back down through the process of emanation (sṛṣṭikrama) as far as the Bindusthāna, one should meditate on Vāgīśvarī in the form of the heart of Vāgīśvara. With the middle finger, using the Utpabha-mudrā, one should place [the deity] within the womb-channel (garbhanāḍī) of Vāgīśvarī while reciting: "oṃ hāṃ haṃ hām ātmane namaḥ. Then, having meditated upon [her] as being united with all the yonis (sarvayoni), one should worship her with the root-mantra (mūla), offer three oblations (āhutitraya), and then... this.

For the sake of the *ātman*, having meditated upon the Lord as being united with the *ātman* at one time within all wombs (*sarvayoni*), and having worshipped Him with the root-mantra (*mūla*) and offered three oblations (*āhuti*), one should petition the Lord, saying: "O Lord, please grant union for this *ātman* with [the Supreme] at one time within all wombs. Thereafter, for the purpose of conception within all wombs, one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra, [saying]: "O Lord, for this *ātman* within all wombs, at one time..."

Having petitioned [the deity], saying, "Please cause the embryo to mature," one should subsequently offer three oblations with the root mantra for this purpose, petitioning, "O Lord, please grant birth to this soul within all wombs. Then, having meditated that [the soul] grows simultaneously within all bodies due to the letter 'A', one should offer three oblations with the root mantra and perform the worldly rites beginning with the tying [of the cord]. This...

Having petitioned the Lord, "May You grant [this] for the Self simultaneously in all bodies," he proceeds to describe the *bhoga-pakva* [offering]. Having meditated upon worldly actions—beginning with wells, ponds, and water-reservoirs—as well as the accumulated (*sañcita*) and prospective (*āgāmī*) karmas, all gathered together in a single place, he offers three oblations (*āhuti*) through the primary channel (*mūla-nāḍī*). [He offers them] to the Lord for this Self, regarding these worldly actions, the accumulated, and the prospective...

Having petitioned that the karmas may remain united within one person, and having performed meditation (*dhyāna*) upon the bodies born from all wombs (*sarvayoni*), he offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra, requesting: "May you perform the purification of karma (*karmārjana*) so as to grant this soul various kinds of enjoyment (*bhoga*) from the Blessed One. Having thus petitioned, subsequently, regarding the objects of the body at the time of death, by means of this fourfold distinction...

While existing as the manifold forms of individual souls (*ānaru*), sustained by the accumulated latent impressions of karma (*sañcita-karmavāsanā*) and so forth, one should meditate upon the experience consisting of the sensations of pleasure and pain; having offered three oblations (*āhuti-traya*) at the root, one should petition the Lord, saying, "May You grant this soul enjoyment within all wombs. At this juncture, one should also perform the forty sacraments (*saṃskāra*) prescribed in the Vedas for the human world, beginning from conception.

He concludes by offering three oblations into the heart. These are: *garbhādhāna*, *puṃsavana*, *sīmantonnayana*, *jātakarman*, *nāmakaraṇa*, *niṣkramaṇa*, *annaprāśana*, *caula*, and *upanayana*—these eleven; the four Vedic vows known as *aiṣṭhika*, *dārvika*, *bhautika*, and *saumika*; and the performance of the five great sacrifices (*pañcamahāyajña*), namely: *godarśana*, *devayajña*, *pitṛyajña*, *bhūtayajña*, *manuṣyayajña*, and *brahmayajña*.

[The text] states that sovereignty arises as the cause... [He] says: the four *pati*s, the *aṣṭakā-parvan*, the *śrāddha*, the *śrāvaṇī*, the *ākāraṇī*, the *maitrī*, and the *āśvayujī*—these seven *pakayajñas*. Otherwise, what? Those [are]: the *agnihotra*, the *darśapūrṇamāsa*, the *ākāraṇa*, the *cāturmāsya*, the *paśubandha*, and the *sautrāmaṇi*—these eight *haviryajñas*. [Then] the *agniṣṭoma*, the *atyagniṣṭoma*, the *ukthya*, the *ṣoḍaśaka*, the *vājapeya*, and the *atirātra*.

Having performed the eighty-four rites—namely, the Aṣṭāptoryāma Soma sacrifices, *medhājñāna*, *vānaprastha*, *parityājya*, and *antyeṣṭi*—he concludes by offering two hundred oblations: three oblations for each individual rite and one hundred and twenty oblations for the eighty-four rites as a whole with the mantra *oṃ haṃ hāṃ hūṃ hṛdayāya svāhā*.

Thereafter, meditating upon the abundant offering of *priyānnavaḍuḍai* (various types of food) during the oblations (*homa*), one should offer three oblations (*āhutitraya*) using the root mantra. Having petitioned, "O Lord, please provide for this self the offering of *mukundavaḍuḍai* in the realm of enjoyment (*bhoga*)," and "O Lord, please grant this self purification from the flow of the effects of *māyā*," one should [perform] the karma that is the cause for enjoyment... [puṅkti...]

Having offered three oblations with a heart that does not turn back from what has been done, one should offer one hundred oblations through the root-mantra (mūla-mantra) in conjunction with the heart-mantra for the purpose of purification regarding birth, lifespan, enjoyment, and impressions (saṃskāra). Then, having prayed to the Lord, "May You grant purity to the Self in all actions," and having meditated upon the Self as being fully revealed, transcending even the power of Māyā so that there is no further worldly enjoyment (bhoga), one should offer three oblations through the root-mantra.

Regarding the objects of enjoyment (*bhoktṛtva-viṣaya*), for the purpose of concealing the impurity of *rūpamāna* through meditation, one should offer ten oblations (*āhuti*) with the root-mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, meditating that the impurity has been cast out, one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra so that the karma already consumed may perish like water; thereafter, meditating that destruction (*nāśa*) has arisen, one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra.

Having offered [the weapon], he should petition the Lord, saying: "O Blessed One, please grant the liberation of this soul from the three bonds known as Māyā, Mala, and Karma. Then, with the *kartarī* blade consecrated seven times with the Astra-mantra, he should strike the head of the power of the Nivṛtti-kalā-bhāva with the mantra: "Oṃ hāṃ nivṛttikalābhāvāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ," together with its form.

Thereafter, for the purpose of releasing the bond (*bandha*), he should join that *pāśa* with both hands using the *astra-mantra*, place it upon the *sruc* ladle which has been filled with clarified butter (*ājya*) using the same *mantra*, and then offer an oblation (*āhuti*) along with the clarified butter while reciting that same *mantra*. Afterward, having offered three oblations with the *astra-mantra*, he shall reduce this [pāśa] to ashes.

Having petitioned the Lord, "O Blessed One, please purify the *nivṛtti-kalā-āvaraṇa* of this self," he should again offer eight oblations (*āhuti*) with the *astra-mantra* while reciting *huṃ*. Then, for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), he should offer as many oblations as possible ending with *svāhā* using the *astra-mantra*, thereby causing the bodies to vanish entirely and meditating that [the self] remains as the singular form of pure consciousness.

Afterwards, if it is a *sabīja-dīkṣā*, one should perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) and worship of Brahmā with the mantra "Brahmaṇe namaḥ. Then, using this same mantra, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with *svāhā*. For the purpose of purifying the eight [senses] (*puryaṣṭaka*), one should offer three oblations with the mantra: "Oṃ hlāṃ brahman śabda-sparśa-śukla-agrahaṇa-svāhā. Then, one should make this request: "O Brahmā, you have performed your duty; please remove all obstacles," thus conveying the command of the Supreme Goddess (*parameśvarī*).

After Brahmā has risen and departed, [the officiant] should perform meditation upon the Self, which remains free from the *nivṛtti-kalā* and *paśu-śakti*, having attained the pure touch of the *liṅga* situated at the level of the *śuddha-tattva*. Then, for the purpose of extracting the Self, he should offer three oblations (*āhutis*) with the root mantra. He should then petition the Lord: "May the Lord graciously extract this Self, having removed it from the *nivṛtti-kalā* and *paśu-śakti*. Om.

Saying "Hāṃ Haṃ Hāṃ Ātmane Namaḥ," having taken up the Self with the *saṃhāramudrā* from the fire at the navel, and having joined it at the middle [of the body] by means of the *pūraka* breath, [one should visualize] the Self as having another location seized by Rāhu... for the purpose of the *paśu-śatru-śāni* [subjugation of enemies], one should join the Self within one's own heart by means of the *recakavāyu*, and having joined it to the remaining subtle body (*sūkṣmadeha*) by means of the *utpattimudrā*, and having worshipped it with the *ātma-mantra*... for the sake of [offering], one should offer a drop of *arghya* water with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.

Having clarified [the mantra] on the ground for the purpose of stabilization (*sthirīkaraṇa*), one should worship the *mūlatrināla* and offer three oblations (*āhuti*). Thereafter, having worshipped Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, one should offer three oblations with their respective *mantratināla* mantras, present the *parāṅmukhārghya*, and perform their awakening (*utthāpana*). Then, while offering the *pūrṇāhuti* with the *vauṣaḍanta-mūlatrināla*, there is the purification of the *nivṛtti-kalā*.

(p.38b, f.35a, l.1) [Pratiṣṭhākalā]: Having joined together the purified kalā and the unpurified kalā as the cause of their union, the nivṛtti-kalā is [assigned] to the end of śuddhamāyā, and the pratiṣṭhā-kalā to the end of nāda: Oṃ hlām hvrīm nivṛttipratiṣṭhāyai namaḥ.

Having joined [the fire] below the navel according to the *Dehasūtra* and worshipped it, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with "svāhā" using this mantra for the purpose of bringing about presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, having performed meditation on the dissolution of the pure state (*śuddhamān-kalā*) into the impure state (*aśuddhamān-kalā*), and having attended upon the *Pratiṣṭhā-kalā*, one should thereafter worship within the fire with "oṃ hām ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ," and offer three oblations with this same mantra for the purpose of bringing about presence. Then, in the *Dehasūtra*...

Having performed meditation on the pervasion of the Yata [mantra] at the location of the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā, one should perform the rite of inspection (nirīkṣaṇa) while reciting: "Oṃ hvīṃ, salutation to Pratiṣṭhā-kalā.

Then, one should recite: "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the waters, fire, wind, ether, smell, taste, form, touch, sound, the organs of generation, excretion, locomotion, grasping, speech, nose, tongue, eyes, skin, ears, mind, ego, intellect, the qualities, and the principles of primordial nature (prakṛti-tattva). Oṃ hāṃ.

Akumāreśa, Prabhāsa, Naimiśa, Puṣkara, Auṣadha, Ḍiṇḍi, Bhārabhūti, Lakulīśa, Hariścandra, Śrīśaila, Jalpeśvara, Āmrādikeśvara, Madhyameśvara, Mahākāla, Kedāra, Bhairava, Gayā, Gurukṣetra, Nākhala, Nakhalā, Vimala, Aṭṭahāsa, Mahendra, Bhīmeśvara, Vastrapāda, Rudrakoṭi, Avimukta, Mahālaya, Gokarṇa, Bhadrakarṇa, Svarṇākṣata, Sthāṇuva, Chagalaṇḍa, Dviraṇḍa, Mārkoṭa, and Maṇḍa.

Salutations to Leśvara, Kālāgni, Śaṅkhukarṇa, Sthūleśvara, Sthaleśvara, Paiśāca, Rākṣasa, Yakṣa, Gandharva, Aindra, Rudra, Saumya, Prājeśa, Brahma, Akṛta, Kṛta, Bhairava, Brahma, Vaiṣṇava, Kaumāra, Saumya, Śrīkaṇṭha, and Bhavānī. And: *Oṃ hāṃ ḷa ha sa ṣa śa va la ra ya ma bha ba pha pa na dha da tha ta ṇa ḍha ḍa ṭha ṭa akṣarebhyo namaḥ* (Salutations to the letters). And: *Oṃ hāṃ śarva*.

Śarva—first, first—release, release—to the Lord of Yoga, obeisance! O Mahātejas, Sadbhāveśvara, Mahādeva, Paramātman, Śarva, Śiva, source of destruction, destruction, non-destruction! Oṃ suvaḥ, oṃ bhuvaḥ, oṃ bhūḥ! Dhū-dhū dhū-dhū! Nānā nānā! O beginningless one, smokeless, smoke-free, fireless, formless! Light, light! Splendor, splendor! First, first! Formless, formless! Pervasive, pervasive!

(1.5) *Namaḥ* to the *padas*. Also, *oṃ hāṃ vāmadevaśivamantrābhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ bījebhyo namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ suṣumnāgāndhārināḍibhyāṃ namaḥ*. (1.6) *Oṃ hāṃ samānodānavāyubhyāṃ namaḥ*. Also, *oṃ hāṃ rasanāpāyuindriyābhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ rasaviṣayāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ hāṃ* (1.7) *rasarūpasparśaśabdaguṇebhyo namaḥ*.

Having performed the nyāsa with "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu, the Lord of Causes," one should meditate on the disciple’s body as being identical to the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*. This [kalā] is white, shaped like a half-moon, and bears the lotus as its emblem; it is associated with the state of sleep (*svapnāvasthā*). Then, having struck [the disciple] below the navel with a flower-stalk while reciting "Oṃ hvīṃ hāṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ," one should recite "Oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ."

Reciting "Pratiṣṭhākalāyai svāhā," perform four times the *śamudra-mudrā* and four times the *pūraka-śakti*, inhaling with "oṃ hauṃ hāṃ hvīṃ hāṃ hauṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai huṃ phaṭ. Perform four times the *saṃhāra-mudrā* and four times the *kumbhaka*, inhaling with "oṃ hāṃ... [and so on].

Saying "Hāṃ, obeisance to the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā," place [the deity] in the pit with the Rēcaka breath and the Utpatti-mudrā. Having worshipped with "Oṃ Hāṃ Hvīṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā" and offered the arghya, offer three oblations ending in *svāhā* while reciting this mantra. Then, performing meditation on the three-fold nature as the Mala-karma, the Āyā-svarūpa, and the Bhoktṛtva-bhoga-śarīra, subsequently recite: "Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu."

Having thus invoked Viṣṇu and worshipped him, one should offer three *saṃnidhāna-āhutis* ending with *svāhā* using this mantra: "O Viṣṇu, within your jurisdiction, I, desiring liberation, am initiating this disciple; O Supreme Goddess, by your command, he must be protected through the root-mantra. The meaning of this is: "O Viṣṇu, within your domain, I am initiating this disciple who aspires for liberation. Thus, by the command of Śiva, one should pray that the Lord be favorable.

Having made this request, and having formed various mental resolves (*saṅkalpa*) within this sacrificial arena (*kalaśa*), one should perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) preceded by meditation upon the Vāgīśvarīs and Vāgīśvaras who pervade it, and worship them. Then, praying that they remain present for the sake of bestowing grace upon oneself, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) with their respective mantras. Having sprinkled the disciple with the Astra-mantra, [one recites]: *oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*.

Having performed the striking with the *nārāca-mudrā* joined together at the heart-channel (*hṛdaya-nāḍī*) along with the flower, [one should] enter through one's own *rāśaka-nāḍī* and the *rāśaka-nāḍī* of the one who has descended [into the disciple], accompanied by the syllable *huṃ*, saying: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ phaṭ*. Then, having exited, [one says]: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ...*

Having taken [the breath] through the four [nostrils] with the *śaṃkha-mudrā* and having recited the *mūla-mantra*, one should lead it to the *dvādaśānta*. Having meditated upon the Self (*ātman*) as being like a drop on the tip of a blade of grass, one should take it back through the four [nostrils] with the *saṃhāra-mudrā* and the *ātma-mantra*. Having placed it within one's own heart during the *pūraka* [breath-retention], one should hold it there (*kumbhita*). Having worshipped the *mūla-mantra* and, following the sequence of abandoning the causal principles beginning with Brahmā along with the mantra, one should again lead it back as far as one's own *dvādaśānta*.

Having brought [the soul] through the sequence of creation as far as the *bindu-sthāna* and caused it to take birth, one should meditate upon the union of Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara. Through the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*) and with the *utpavamudrā*, [one should recite]: "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hām ātmane namaḥ. Having placed [the soul] within the womb-channel (*garbhanāḍī*) of Vāgīśvarī, one should meditate on the Self as being united with all matrices (*sarvayoni*). Having worshipped with the root mantra (*mūlamantreṇa*) and offered three oblations (*āhutitraya*), [one should pray]: "O Lord, for this Self..."

Having petitioned that the Self (ātman) be granted birth within all wombs, and having meditated upon it as growing simultaneously within all bodies for the sake of its authority, one offers three oblations (āhuti) through the root-nāḍī. Then, having petitioned that the Lord (bhagavān) grant this Self the state of growing simultaneously within all bodies, one states the cause for its departure: "It becomes a Vedic rite beginning with the purificatory rites (saṃskāra) such as those of Soma."

Having meditated upon the karmas beginning with those born of *kṛcchra* penance that exist in a single location, he offers three oblations (*āhutis*) with the *mūla-mantra*. Then, having petitioned the Lord, "May all these accumulated karmas of this self, beginning with [those] existing in a single location, be gathered together," [he performs the rite] in all the bodies of various wombs (*yoni*).

Having performed meditation on the *nāḍī* that bestows enjoyment (*bhoga*), one offers three oblations (*āhuti*) into the *mūla-nāḍī*, making this petition: "O Blessed One, please grant the purification of karma (*karmārjana*) which bestows various kinds of enjoyment upon this self. Then, according to the distinctions of place, time, body, and object... ... [as per p. 41a, l. 1] ... (Note: The ellipsis indicates the continuation of the ritual procedure regarding the specific parameters of the offering.)

Having meditated upon the Lord, who exists as the essence of the experience of pleasure and pain through the latent impressions (*vāsanā*) of accumulated and being-performed actions (*sañcita-karmāgamyamāna-karma*), which have taken hold of the form (*rūpa*), and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the *mūla-mantra*, one should petition the Lord: "May the Lord bring about the ripening of the experiences (*bhoga-paripāka*) for this self within all womb-born bodies. Then, having performed great acts of endearment and affection toward Him, one should offer three oblations with the *mūla-mantra* to the Lord... for this [self].

Having petitioned, "May [the Lord] grant the abundance of enjoyment for the Self," one offers three oblations (āhutis) through the Mūlādhāra for the purification of the effects of Māyā. Then, having petitioned, "May the Blessed One grant the purification of the flow of the effects of Māyā for this Self," and having performed the recitation (japa), one offers three oblations through the Hṛdaya so that the karma accumulated may be consumed and there be no possibility of returning again. Afterward—

For the sake of purifying [the soul] from birth, lifespan, enjoyment, latent impressions (*saṃskāra*), and so forth, one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra joined at the head by *oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hauṃ śivāya svāhā*. Having prayed to the Lord, "May You grant purification for this soul in all its actions," and having meditated upon the soul as being liberated from the power of Māyā so that there is no further rebirth, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra regarding the objects of the status of the enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*).

Having performed meditation on the impurity that constitutes one's own nature (*svarūpābhāsa-mala-kārya*) for the purpose of its concealment (p. 41b, f. 38a, l. 1), one should offer ten oblations (*daśāhuti*) with the root mantra *oṃ hāṃ paṃ śuṃ hauṃ śivāya svāhā*. Then, having meditated upon the impurity as having been cast out from the body, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. Having meditated that the karma of eating has been completely destroyed, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. [Then] to the Lord... this...
