Having petitioned that the three bonds (*pāśatraya*), which are said to be the impurity (*mala*) of the Self, must be severed, he should subsequently join [the soul] to the "opening" (*vellai*) of the bond of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*—which has been consecrated (*abhimantrita*) seven times with the *asthiti-nāl* and the *kartari-nāl* accompanied by the mantra-form *oṃ hvīṃ pratiṣṭhākalāpāśāya huṃ phaṭ*. Afterwards, for the purpose of liberating it from bondage, he should [seize] that bond with both hands.

Having gathered [the materials] with the *astramantra*, having rubbed them with clarified butter (*ājya*), and having offered [them] into the fire along with that clarified butter using the final mantra, one should burn them.

Thereafter, having offered three oblations with the Astra-mantra (l. 7), he requests the Lord: "May You grant this soul the attainment of *pratiṣṭhā* (stability). Then, so that His own noose (*pāśa*) may not be released, he offers five oblations with the Astra-mantra while uttering "Hum" (l. 8). Finally, for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), he offers eight oblations with the Astra-mantra. [The text continues from the beginning of page 42b, following a blank on page 42a.]

Even while the bodies remain vacant, one should perform meditation [dhyāna] upon Viṣṇu, whose consciousness remains of a single form. Reciting *oṃ haṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*, one performs the invocation (*āvāhana*) and worships Viṣṇu. Then, with this same mantra, ending with *svāhā*, one offers three oblations (*āhuti*). For the purpose of purifying the eight cities (*puryaṣṭaka-śuddhi*), one offers three oblations with the mantra: *oṃ hāṃ hvīṃ viṣṇor āsyaṃ śuklaṃ gṛhāṇa svāhā*. O... [bho].

"O Viṣṇu, you must ensure that the traveler attains the state of freedom from affliction; this is the command of the Supreme Goddess," thus petitioning and raising up Viṣṇu, one should then meditate upon the Self as residing within the pure principle (*śuddhatattva*), seated upon pure crystal, having emerged from the power of the moment of installation (*pratiṣṭhākālāśakti*) and remaining liberated. Then, for the purpose of returning [the deity] once again, one should offer three oblations (*āhutitraya*) with the root mantra (*mūlamantreṇa*).

Having thus petitioned the Lord, "Please accept this self after it has been established," he removes the self from the fire. Then, by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, he takes the self—which is the size of a thumb and remains with the color of the half-moon—as it is being filled with breath (*pūraka*), and brings it into his own heart. Then, with the *reca* [breath] and the *utpatti-mudrā*, he joins it to the thread-body (*sūtra-deha*) of the disciple.

Having worshipped [the deity], for the purpose of *āpyāyana* (satiating), one should sprinkle drops of *arghya* water upon the head of the sacrificer (*yāvan*) with the root-mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. Then, for the purpose of *strīkaraṇa* (feminization), one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root-mantra. Afterwards, having worshipped Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, one should offer three oblations with their respective root-mantras; then, having offered the *parānmukha-arghya* and performed their *utthāpana* (elevation), one should offer the *pūrṇāhuti* with the root-mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*.
This is the purification of the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā* (Vidyākalā).
(Vidyākalā) (l. 2)

One should utter the mantra *oṃ hvīṃ hūṃ pratiṣṭhāvidyābhyāṃ namaḥ*, dissolving the pure Pratiṣṭhā-kalā into the end of Śuddhamāyā and the impure Vidyā-kalā into the end of Nāda. Having worshipped at the station of the Vidyā-kalā, one should offer three oblations (*āhutis*) ending in *svāhā* with this mantra for the sake of its presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, meditating that it has been dissolved into the Śuddhamāyā-kalā, one performs the rite of elevation (*utthāpana*) of the Vidyā-kalā. Afterward, [one recites]: *oṃ hām ādhāraśaktaye*.

Having worshipped the Ādhāra-śakti in the fire with "Namaḥ," one should offer three oblations ending in svāhā using this mantra for the purpose of invocation (*sannidhāna*). Then, performing the *nirīkṣaṇa* (inspection), one should establish the station of its pervasion (*vyāpti*) within the body of the thread during the placement of the Vidyā-kalā (*vidyākalānyāsa*), reciting: "Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vidyā-kalā."

Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principles (tattvas) of Puruṣa, Rāga, Vidya, Kalā, Niyati, Kāla, and Māyā. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the worlds (bhuvanās) of Bhīma, Ugra, Bhava, Īśāna, Ekavīra, Pracaṇḍa, Umāpati, Aja, Ananta, Ekaśikha, Kodhana, Caṇḍa, Jyotis, Saṃvarta, Lakulīśvara, Pañcāntaka, Ekavīra, Śikheta, Mahādyuti, Mahātejas, Vāmadeva, Bhavaudbhava, Ekapiṅga, Ekekṣaṇa, Īśāna, and Aṅguṣṭhamātraka. Oṃ hāṃ Ña Jha Ja Cha Ca.

Oṃ, homage to the letters Ṅ and GHA. Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to the pervasive one, the pervasive one, the space-like one, the space-like one, who is intent upon the Supreme Lord who is both insentient and sentient, whose form is light, and who is the sovereign of all knowledge.

To the one presiding over all yoga, to the deathless protector, to the one more secret than the secret: *Oṃ*, salutations again and again. To the one whose form is Sadyojāta, to the secret Vāmadeva, to the Aghora heart, to the Tatpuruṣa face, to the Īśāna head, to Śiva, the source of all: *Oṃ*, salutations to Śiva. Salutations to the words that take away [mental] distraction. And: *Oṃ hāṃ huṃ haṃ*, salutations to the two mantras, Śiva and Aghora. *Oṃ hām*, salutations to the two immortal seeds (*amara-bīja*). And: *Oṃ hām a...*

Salutation to the two channels of the *puruṣa*. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vyāna and the serpent [Vāsuki]. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the hand and the organ of sight. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to form and the object of perception. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the qualities of form, touch, and sound. And likewise: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Rudra and the Lord of Causes (*kāraṇeśvara*).

Having thus performed the nyāsa, one should meditate on the Vidyākalā—who remains as a red-colored, triangular maṇḍala adorned with svastikas, and who possesses the state of deep sleep (suṣupti)—as being distinct from the body and the thread of the disciple. Then, reciting *oṃ hāṃ hūṃ vidyākalāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, one should perform the striking (*tāḍana*) with flowers upon the thread of the vessel. Finally, [one recites]: *oṃ hāṃ hrūṃ vidyākalāyai svāhā*.

Having thus drawn [the breath] four times with the *aṅkuśamudrā* and four times with the *pūraka*, [one recites]: *oṃ hauṃ hāṃ hrūṃ hāṃ hauṃ vidyākalāyai huṃ phaṭ*. Having thus drawn [the breath] four times with the *saṃhāramudrā* and four times with the *aṅkuśamudrā*, [one recites]: *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ vidyākalāyai namaḥ*.

Having placed the Ādhāraśakti in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) with the Rēcakatithi-mudrā and Utpavamudrā, and having worshipped her with "oṃ hāṃ vidyākalāyai namaḥ" and offered arghya, one should offer three oblations for the presence (sannidhāna) ending with svāhā using this mantra. Then, performing meditation on the three bonds (pāśas)—namely mala, karma, and māyā—which produce the nature of the enjoyer (bhoktṛtva) and the body of enjoyment (bhogaśarīra), one thereafter [offers] "oṃ hāṃ rudrāya namaḥ."

Having performed the invocation (*āvāhana*) of Rudranetra with [the mantra] "... and having worshipped him, one offers three oblations for his presence (*sannidhāna-āhuti*) with "oṃ hāṃ niya svāhā. Then, one makes this petition: "O Rudra, I am under your authority; desiring liberation, I shall initiate this disciple. May you, O Lord, be favorable toward me through your supreme command. The meaning of this is: "In your jurisdiction, O Rudranetra, I intend to initiate this willing disciple; therefore, may you be well-disposed toward me according to the will of Śiva. Having thus requested, [one contemplates] the various forms of wombs (*yoni*) within this *kalā*.

Having visualized [the deities] pervading that [space], and having performed the invocation (*āvāhana*) preceded by meditation upon the assembly of Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, and having worshipped them, one offers three oblations (*āhuti*) with the mantra-tattva. Then, praying, "May you remain present for the sake of bestowing grace upon the self," one sprinkles the disciple with the weapon-tattva (*astra-tattva*), saying *oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, while using the flower-tattva (*puṣpa-tattva*) and the nārāca-mudrā at the region of the heart.

Having performed the *tāḍana* [striking], one should enter the disciple’s body through the *rēcakatī-nāl̤ai* [channel of exhalation] with the sound *huṃ*. Then, reciting *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, and again *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā*, one should withdraw [the consciousness] by means of the *śaṅkha-mudrā*. Having chanted the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) and led [the soul] to the *dvādaśānta* [twelfth center] of the disciple, one should meditate upon the Self (*ātman*) as having the form of a drop on the tip of a red lotus stalk (*ruṇāgra-bindu-rūpa*). Then: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ ātmane namaḥ*.

Having thus received [the breath] through the saṃhāramudrā in four counts and brought it into one's own heart by means of pūraka in four counts, having retained it there, and having recited the mūlamantra together with the ātmamantra, one should proceed according to the sequence of the renunciation of the causes beginning with Brahmā, leading it up to the limit of one’s own dvādaśānta; then, returning again by the sequence of creation to the limit of the piṇḍasthāna, one should meditate upon the pitcher of Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, and [the breath] should emerge through the left nāḍī in four counts.

With the *utpava-mudrā*, reciting *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hām ātmane namaḥ*, one places [the mantra] within the womb of Vāgīśvarī. Then, having performed the meditation on the soul (*ātma-dhyāna*) as being united with all wombs (*sarvayoni*), one worships with the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*), offers three oblations (*āhuti-traya*), and makes this petition: "O Blessed One, please grant that this soul may attain the state of a *kakuḍa* (emancipated) in a single lifetime within all wombs. This is for the sake of the birth of the womb-state (*garbhatva*) that has arisen within all wombs.

Having offered three oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, the Lord petitioned that this self might attain the state of being in the womb (*garbhatva*) within all wombs (*sarvayoni*) at once; thereafter, He petitioned that birth (*janman*) be granted. Then, for the sake of authority (*adhikāra*), He petitioned that growth be brought about simultaneously within all bodies. Finally, for the purpose of bringing about the ripening of the departure (*bhoga-pakvīkaraṇa*), [He entered] as the Vaiśya-janman, becoming the internal self (*ādhyātmika*).

Having performed meditation upon all accumulated (*sañcita*), prospective (*āgāmī*), and existing (*vartamāna*) karmas taken together, and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) into the root fire, one should petition: "O Lord, please perform the purification of this self's karma that bestows worldly enjoyment (*bhoga*)—whether pertaining to the self (*ādhyātmika*), the accumulated, the prospective, or the existing. Then, one should perform the purification of karma that bestows various kinds of enjoyment according to the distinctions of place, time, body, and object.

Having petitioned, "Please grant [this]," and having assumed various forms through the distinctions of place, time, and body—remaining as accumulated and non-accumulated karmic impressions (saṃcitāgāmīya-karmavāsanā)—one should perform meditation on the experience consisting of pleasant and painful sensations. Then, having offered three oblations (āhuti-traya) at the root, one should petition: "Please grant the ripening of experience for this Self in all other locations. Thus, regarding the objects of experience (bhogya), the most...

Having petitioned, "O Beloved One, please grant the purification for the commencement of the Mahāmāyā-kārya," he offers three oblations (*āhuti*) with the *mūla-mantra*. Then, having petitioned, "O Blessed One, please grant this soul the purification for the commencement of the Mahāmāyā-kārya," and having caused [the soul] to consume the karmas that serve as the cause for its departure (*bhoga*), he likewise offers three oblations with the *hṛdaya-mantra* according to what was previously stated.

For the purpose of purifying [the self] from birth, lifespan, experience (*bhoga*), latent impressions (*saṃskāra*), and so forth, one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra accompanied by the *śikhā* mantra: *oṃ hāṃ haiṃ hauṃ śivāya svāhā*. Having thus petitioned that the purity of this self be granted for all ritual acts (*sarvakarmasu*), one should meditate upon the self as having emerged from Mahāmāyā-Śakti in such a way that there is no further experience (*bhoga*). Then, offering three oblations with the root mantra, one should abandon attachment toward the objects of the status of the enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva-viṣayeṣu*).

(1.3) Having performed meditation upon the impurity of *svarūpājñāna* (ignorance of one's true nature), which is the cause of karma, for the purpose of its concealment, one should offer ten oblations (*āhuti*) with the *Paśupatāstra-mantra* together with the root mantra. Then, having meditated upon that [impurity] as having been cast out from the root mantra, one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. Even if one has caused the karma to be consumed, one should meditate directly upon the birth of destruction [of that karma] by offering three oblations with the root mantra, [thinking]: "O Lord, this karma is the impurity of this self."

Having petitioned that the release of the three bonds (*pāśatraya*) as previously described be graciously granted, he then, in the manner of a *yati*, while consecrating with the *astra-mantra* using the *kartarī-mudrā*, recites the mantra-form: *oṃ hūṃ vidyākalāpāśāya haḥ hūṃ phaṭ*. Having thus purified the bond of the *vidyākalā-pāśa* at its junction, he then breaks that bond for the purpose of removing the fetters (*bandhaka*), and shakes it off with his hands while brandishing the *astramudrā*.

Having placed [the offering] in the *sruc* ladle filled with clarified butter (*ājya*), he performs the oblation (*homa*) while reciting that mantra ending with *svāhā*, accompanied by the *ājya*. While burning it, he subsequently offers three oblations (*āhutitraya*) with the *astra-mantra*, thereby reducing it to ashes.

Having petitioned the Lord, "May You please purify this self of the impurity of ignorance," one should offer five oblations with the Astra-mantra for the sake of the cessation of the impurities of this [self]. Then, as a concluding expiation (prāyaścitta), one offers eight oblations with the Astra-mantra. Having performed this, one should meditate that all the bodies have vanished and remain only as a single form of consciousness (caitanya). Then, one should worship Rudra with the mantra: *oṃ hāṃ rudrāya namaḥ*.

Having performed the invocation (*āvāhana*) and worship, and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with *svāhā* for the sake of the presence (*sannidhāna*), one should offer three oblations for the purification of the eightfold mantra (*puryaṣṭaka-śuddhi*) with: *oṃ hāṃ rudrarūpakandhau śuklaṃ gṛhāṇa svāhā*. Then, having petitioned Śivāñjeyī with: "O Rudra, by you [this] disease-free state of my own self must be secured"—thus giving the command—one should awaken Rudra. Afterwards, for the one stationed at the head of the pure principle (*śuddhatattvāgra-sthāya*)...

Having meditated upon the Self as being like a pure crystal gem, situated within the Vidyākalāpāśa, and having extracted it from the fire by means of the three oblations (*āhuti*) offered with the *mūla-mantra* for the purpose of re-extraction, one should petition the Lord, saying, "May the Lord extract this Self from the Vidyākalāpāśa," and then extract it from the fire with the *ātma-mantra* and the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, while performing the *pūraka* breath-retention in the intermediate space.

Having brought the soul—which has been released by Rāhu during the *ardhacandra* [phase] and whose life-span is being consumed by Saturn—into his own heart, he should place it within the *dehasūtra* of the disciple's body using the *utpavamudrā* along with the *repha*. Having worshipped it, he should sprinkle drops of *arghya* water upon the head of the disciple with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* for the purpose of nourishment (*āpyāyana*). Then, for the sake of stabilization (*sthirīkaraṇa*), he should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra. After that...

Having worshipped Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara (p. 47a, l. 1), they offer three oblations (āhuti) with the mantra, bestow the *parānmukhārghya*, and having raised [the deity], they offer the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ* (or *vauṣaḍanta*). This is the purification of the *vidyākala*. While purifying the *vidyākala*, one should pronounce it up to the end of *māyā*; and while purifying the *śāntikala*, which is impure, one should pronounce it up to the end of *nāda*.

Having worshipped with "Oṃ Hrūṃ Hyaiṃ, salutations to Vidyā and Śānti" at the station of the Śāntikalā, one should offer three *sannidhāna*-oblations using this mantra. Then, meditating upon the purified Vidyākalā as being dissolved into the purified Śāntikalā, one should perform the *upasthāna* of the Śāntikalā at its respective station. Afterwards, [one offers]: "Oṃ Hāṃ, salutations to Ādhāraśakti."

Having thus worshipped in the fire and offered three oblations ending with *svāhā* while reciting "I am present here," one should perform the visualization of its pervasive extension at the location of the *śāntikalā* on the body-thread, reciting: *oṃ hyaiṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ*. Then, while gazing [at it], one should recite: *oṃ hāṃ śuddhavidyeśvarasadāśivatattvebhyo namaḥ*.

Om Hāṃ. Salutations to Mano-manī, Sarva-bhūta-damana, Bala-pramathinī, Bala-vikaraṇī, Kala-vikaraṇī, Kālī, Raudrī, Jyeṣṭhā, Vāmā, Śikhaṇḍī, Śrīkaṇṭha, Trimūrti, Ekarudra, Ekanetra, Śivottama, Sūkṣma, Ananta, and Sadāśiva; salutations to the worlds.

Oṃ hāṃ ga kha ka varṇebhyo namaḥ. Also: Oṃ hāṃ dhyānaharāya nityaṃ yogine yogapīṭhasaṃsthitāya śāśvatāya dhruvāya anāśritāya anāthāya anantāya śivāya sarvavyāpine vyomarūpāya vyomavyāpine padebhyo namaḥ. Oṃ hāṃ heṃ haiṃ tatpuruṣakavaktrebhyo namaḥ. Oṃ hāṃ bindu yakārabījābhyāṃ namaḥ.

Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Alaplaṣaka and the two *nāḍīs*. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kūrma and the wind (*vāyu*). Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the skin and the sense organ of touch. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the object of touch and its sphere. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the quality of touch and sound. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Īśvara and Kāraṇeśvara.

Having thus performed the nyāsa, one should meditate on the *śāntikalā*, which possesses a mouth adorned with a dot (*bindu*) and marked by a six-cornered [figure], black in color, and situated in a state of extreme difficulty (*duryavasthā*). Then, performing the meditation on the distinction between the disciple’s body and the thread, one should strike it with a flower-stalk below the *prūmadhya* while reciting: *oṃ hāṃ haiṃ hāṃ śāntikalāyai huṃ phaṭ*. Then: *oṃ hāṃ haiṃ hāṃ śāntikalāyai svāhā*.

Having inhaled four times through the *śamudrī* mudrā while reciting "Oṃ hauṃ hāṃ hauṃ śāntikalāyai huṃ phaṭ," and having held [the breath] with *kumbhaka* while performing the *saṃhāra* mudrā, and then having exhaled four times through *recaka* while reciting "Oṃ hāṃ haiṃ hāṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ" while performing the *utpatti* mudrā, one should place [the fire] within the pit upon the *ādhāraśakti*. Then, [one should offer oblations] while reciting "Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ."

Having worshipped thus and offered the *arghya*, one should perform three oblations (*sannidhānāhuti*) with this mantra ending in *svāhā*. Then, meditating that Mahāmāyā—who is the presiding deity over authority, impurity, and pure action—is the very nature of the Self, one should contemplate how She brings about the three fetters (*pāśatraya*), the three-fold reality (*tripakṣatattva*), and the body consisting of the limbs of enjoyment (*bhogāṅga-śarīra*). [Then recite: *Oṃ hāṃ īśvarakāraṇeśvarāya namaḥ*.

Thus (p. 48a, l. 1), having invoked and worshipped Īśvara, one performs three oblations ending with *svāhā* for the purpose of bringing about his presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, one makes this petition: "I am one who holds authority over the *Īśāna-tattva*, and desiring liberation, I shall initiate [this disciple]. O Supreme Lord, by Your command, You must be favorable toward me. The meaning of this is as follows: having requested the Lord, "Please unite this disciple within the state of Śiva," and having prayed, "May You be favorable," one [performs] many various kinds [of rites] within that *kalā*.

Having mentally conceived the *yoginīs*, one should perform their invocation (*āvāhana*) preceded by meditation upon the pervasive Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara within them, and having worshipped them, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with *svāhā* using their respective mantras for the purpose of their presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, having prayed, "May you remain present so as to bestow grace upon me," and having sprinkled the disciple with the *astra-mantra*, [one should recite] "oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ" at the location of the heart.

Having performed the *tāḍana* (striking) with the *puṣpatināla* and the *kūṭīn nārācamudrā*, one should enter the body of the disciple through one's own *rekhakati* (channel of the line) along with the syllable *huṃ*, reciting: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ*. Then, reciting *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā*, one should withdraw [the consciousness] by means of the *śamudrā* and, having chanted the root mantra (*mūlamantra*), proceed with the twelve-fold purification (*dvādaśānta*). One should then meditate upon the Self in the form of a drop (*bindu*) at the tip of the nose, reciting: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hām*.

Saying "ātmane namaḥ," having received [the breath] through the saṃhāramudrā for four counts, and having brought it into one's own heart via pūraka for four counts, one should hold it there (kumbhita) while reciting the mūlamantra...

Having performed the recitation (*japa*) with the *ātma-mantra*, one should proceed by the sequence of renunciation (*tyāga*) starting from Brahmā up to the limit of the twelve [centers], and then return again by the sequence of emanation (*sr̥ṣṭi*) down to the limit of the bindu. Having thus projected [the mantra] outward, one should meditate upon the union of Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara. Then, through the middle channel and the *utpava-mudrā*, one should place [the mantra] within the *garbha-nāḍī* of Vāgīśvarī, reciting: *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hām ātmane namaḥ*.

Having performed meditation on the union of the self with all wombs (*sarvayoni*) at one time, having worshipped with the *mūlatrīṇāla* mantra, and having offered three oblations (*āhutitraya*), one should petition the Lord, saying: "May the Lord grant this self union with all wombs at one time. Then, for the sake of the conception and birth of the embryo that has arisen within the bodies of all wombs, one should offer three oblations with the *mūlatrīṇāla* mantra, [petitioning] the Lord: "For this self, in all wombs at one time..."

Having petitioned that [the Lord] should grant birth, one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) upon the fact that, by virtue of the authority [of the mantra], it grows at every moment within all bodies that are completely pure; then, having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the *mūla-mantra*, one should petition the Blessed One that He should grant growth at every moment for this self within all bodies. Then, for the sake of attaining liberation (*bhoga*), one should offer [oblations] for the removal of the *ādhyātmika*, *sañcita*, and *āgāmī* [karmas].

Having meditated upon the conjunction of all karmas within a single locus, one offers three oblations with the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*). Then, having petitioned the Lord, saying, "May these accumulated and non-accumulated karmas belonging to this self be gathered together into one," one meditates upon the cleansing of karma that grants enjoyment simultaneously across bodies born from all wombs. Having offered three oblations with the root-mantra, [one addresses] the Lord... this... (Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly; the translation reflects the available portion.)

Having petitioned that the Lord should grant the purification of pure karma (*śuddhakarmārjana*) which bestows various kinds of enjoyment (*bhoga*) upon the Self, [the practitioner] offers three oblations (*āhuti-traya*) into the Root [Fire], meditating upon the latent impressions of karma (*karmavāsanā*)—which exist as accumulated and non-accumulated (*sañcita-āgāmīya*) and possess various forms according to the distinctions of place, time, body, and subject—that consist of the experience of pleasure and pain. To this Self, the Lord [bestows...]

Having petitioned that [the Lord] should grant the ripening of enjoyments (*bhoga-paripāka*) in all worlds, and having meditated upon the supreme nectar of intense delight in objects of enjoyment (*bhogya*), one offers three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root mantra. Then, petitioning the Blessed One that He should grant this self the supreme nectar of intense delight in objects of enjoyment, one offers three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the purification of the flow of Mahāmāyā... for this self.

Having made the request, "May you grant the purification of the flow [of the fire] initiated by Mahāmāyā," one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) into the heart-channel for the sake of liberation, so that the karmas which are the cause of transmigratory existence may not lead to a return. Then, for the purpose of purifying birth, lifespan, experience, and impressions (*saṃskāra*), one should offer three oblations into the root-channel accompanied by the armor-mantra (*kavacamantreṇa sahitaḥ*), reciting: *oṃ hāṃ haiṃ hāṃ śivāya svāhā*. [Then one says: "O Blessed One, for this self..."

Having requested, "May purity be granted in all rites," one should perform meditation (*dhyāna*) on the Self as being revealed even while remaining within the power of *māyā*, according to the fourfold [mantra] without distinction; then, having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the root-mantra, one should perform meditation on the impurity of the *adhikāra* (office/qualification), which consists in the very nature of the state of being an enjoyer (*bhoktṛtva*) and the state of being an object of experience (*viṣayatva*), [and thus effect] its concealment (* tirodhāna*).

Reciting "Oṃ ślīṃ paśuṃ haṃ sivāya svāhā," one offers ten oblations with the *pāśupatāstra-mantra* using the root mantra. (L. 4) One should meditate on [the soul] as having arisen from the *adhikāramala*. Then, offering three oblations with the root mantra, one petitions the Lord: "Please sever these three bonds (*pāśatraya*) for this soul—namely, *adhikāramala*, *mahāmāyā*, and *śuddhakarmasvarūpa*. Thereafter, with the *astra-mantra*, one sprinkles the sacrificial vessel (*kartarī*) which has been consecrated sevenfold. (L. 6)

With the mantra-form *oṃ haiṃ śāntikalāpāśāya haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, one should destroy the bond of the Śāntikalā-Śakti within its enclosure; thereafter, for the purpose of removing that bond, having pierced that bond, and having placed it in a *sruc* ladle filled with clarified butter (*ājya*) while forming the four hands as the four weapons (*astra*), one should burn it by performing a *homa* with that same mantra, accompanied by clarified butter and ending with *svāhā*.

Afterwards, having offered three oblations with the Astra-mantra, one should reduce [the deity] to ashes. Then, having petitioned the Lord, saying, "May You grant this soul the grace of the Śāntikalā-pāśa-cheda," one should offer three oblations with the Astra-mantra while uttering "Hum Phaṭ" for the purpose of removing that very pāśāṅkura. Furthermore, for the sake of expiation (prāyaścitta), having offered eight oblations with the Astra-mantra, one should cause all bodies to be completely destroyed.

Having meditated upon [the deity] as being in the form of a cloud of consciousness (*caitanya-megha-rūpa*), one should then perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) of Īśvara with the mantra *oṃ hām īśvarāya namaḥ* and worship Him. By means of this same mantra, one should offer three oblations for the purpose of making [the deity] present (*sannidhāna-huti*). Then, for the sake of purifying the intellect and ego of Īśvara, one should offer three oblations with the mantra: *oṃ hām īśvara-buddhy-ahaṅkāra-śuddhy-arthaṃ gṛhāṇa svāhā*. [Finally, one should pray: "O Īśvara! You must remove all obstacles on the path of this practitioner so that he may attain the state free from affliction."

Having petitioned Śiva with the command "O Supreme Goddess of these [mantras]," and having awakened Īśvara, one should meditate upon the Self as residing within the pure principle (śuddhatattva), seated upon a pure crystal, and abiding there as the power (śakti) of the tranquil digit (śāntikalā). Then, for the purpose of drawing out the fire from its place, one should offer three oblations (āhuti) into the root channel (mūlanāḍī) and [offer] this Self to the Lord.

Having petitioned that the power of the *śāntikalā* be bestowed, [one should] take up the *ātman* from the fire of the *ātma-mantra*... (l. 7) by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā*. Then, in the middle [of the body], together with the *pūraka* [breath], at the time of Rāhu... (l. 8) having risen and emerged, one brings the *ātman*, which is equal in size to the moon-disk, into one’s own heart; then, together with the *recaka* [breath], by means of the *utpatti-mudrā*, one places it within the *sūtra-deha* of the disciple. (l. 9)

Having worshipped [the disciple], one should sprinkle water from the *arghya* vessel upon the head of the disciple for the purpose of *āpyāyana* (nourishment), reciting the root mantra ending with *vauṣaṭ*. Then, for the purpose of making them female (*strīkaraṇa*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra. Afterwards, having prayed to Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, one should offer three oblations with the mantra ending in *svāhā*, present the *parāṅmukha-arghya*, and perform their elevation (*utthāpana*).
Finally, one should offer the *pūrṇāhuti* with the root mantra ending in *vauṣaṭ*. This is the purification of the *śāntikalā*.

One should pronounce the *śuddhamāyā* kalā as ending with *māyā*, and the *aśuddhamāyā* kalā as ending with *nāda*, followed by the *śāntyatīta* kalā. (l. 4) Having worshipped at the station of the *śāntyatīta* kalā with the mantra: "oṃ hyaiṃ hauṃ śāntiśāntyatītābhyāṃ namaḥ," one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with *svāhā* using this same mantra for the purpose of invoking its presence (*sannidhāna*). Then, having performed meditation on the dissolution of the *śuddhamāyā* kalā into the *aśuddhamāyā* kalā, [one should place] the *śāntyatīta* kalā in its own station. (l. 5)

Having performed the *uddhāpana* (invocation), one should worship in the fire with "oṃ hāṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ. Then, with this mantra, one should offer three *sannidhāna-āhutis*. Next, in the location of the *śāntyatīta-kalā* within the body of the thread (*sūtradeha*), one should perform meditation on its pervasive extension with "oṃ hāṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ" while gazing [upon it]. [Then recite: "oṃ hāṃ śaktitatvābhyāṃ namaḥ."

Oṃ hāṃ, salutations to the worlds of Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Kalā, Śānti, Śāntyatītā, Āndhikā, Dīpikā, Rocikā, Mocikā, and Ūrdhvagāminī; to the one whose form is space (vyomarūpa); to the infinite, the protectorless, and the supportless. Also: Oṃ hāṃ aḥ aṃ au o ai e ḷ ḷ ṝ ṛ ū u ī i ā a, salutations to the phonemes (varṇa). Also: Oṃ hāṃ oṃ, salutations to the word (pada). Oṃ hāṃ hoṃ haḥ hauṃ, salutations to the mantras of Īśāna... Śiva. Oṃ hāṃ... [and so forth].

Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kāra and Bīja. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kuhu and Śaṅkinī-nāḍī. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Devadatta and Vāyu. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vāk and the sense of hearing. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the object of sound. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the quality of sound. And likewise: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sadāśiva, the Lord of Causes.

Having performed the nyāsa thus, one should meditate upon the Śāntyātīta-kalā as being beyond the [other] kalās, possessing a smoky color and a swollen form, adorned with a vessel of nectar, and having merged it into oneself. Then, performing the meditation on the difference between the disciple’s heart, body, and the thread, one should strike [the thread] below the Brahma-randhra with a flower while reciting: *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ hāṃ śāntyātīta-kalāyai huṃ phaṭ*. Then: *oṃ haḥ hauṃ*.

Reciting "HĀṂ ŚĀNTYĀTĪTAKALĀYAI HUṂ PHAṬ," perform the *saṃhāramudrā* four times and draw [the energy] up through the *kumbhaka* four times. Reciting "OṂ HĀṂ HAUṂ HĀṂ ŚĀNTYĀTĪTAKALĀYAI NAMAḤ," perform the *utpattimudrā* with the *recaka* breath and place it within the *kuṇḍa* into the *śakti*, which is the nature of the *ādhāra*. Recite: "OṂ HĀṂ HAUṂ HĀṂ ŚĀNTYĀTĪTAKALĀYAI NAMAḤ."

Having thus worshipped and offered the *arghya*, and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) ending with "svāhā" while reciting "iti nāle sannidhāna," one should perform meditation, thinking: "I am the presiding authority; I am performing the purification of karma and the Great Māyā-form; I shall bring about the three-fold bond (*pāśatraya*) and the cessation of worldly enjoyment (*bhoga*). Then, reciting "oṃ hāṃ sadāśivāya namaḥ," one should invoke (*āvāhana*) Sadāśiva, worship Him, and offer three oblations ending with "sannidhāna" while reciting "iti nāle. [Then recite: "I am the authority of Sadāśiva; desiring liberation, I shall initiate [the disciple]. I am to become... [bhāvya].

"By you, O Supreme Lord, acting in accordance with [my] command... (The meaning of this is: "O Blessed One, O Sadāśiva, having initiated a disciple who desires liberation within your divine office, and having performed the rite of *nirodha* by means of the *Śivāñjali*, may Your Honor be favorable"—having thus petitioned, one should, within that *kalā*, form the resolve (*saṅkalpa*) for various kinds of numerous births, and then perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) preceded by meditation upon the pervasive Vāgīśvarī and the assembly of Vāgīśvaras.

Having worshipped them, he offers three oblations ending with *svāhā* using the *mantratināla*. (l. 4) Having prayed, "May you remain present for the sake of bestowing grace upon me," he sprinkles the disciple with the *astratināla*, saying *oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ* (l. 5). Then, having joined [the hands] with the *puṣpatināla* at the region of the heart and performed the striking (*tāḍana*) with the *nārācamudrā*, he [projects] the *huṃkāra* together with his own *reśaka* into the body of the disciple (l. 6).

Having entered with "oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ," and having drawn [the breath] four times with the *śaṃ* mudrā while reciting "oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā," one should take the root mantra and lead it as far as the twelve-finger space from the heart. Having performed the meditation on the serpent in the form of a drop at the tip of a blade of grass (*tṛṇāgrabindurūpanāgadhyāna*), one should draw it back four times with the *saṃhāra* mudrā. Having brought it back into one's own heart during the fourth inhalation (*pūraka*) and placed it there, one should retain it (*kumbhita*) while reciting the root mantra. . . . . . . ?

Having proceeded through the fourfold sequence of causes beginning with Brahmā up to the extent of his own twelve [fingers], and having returned again through the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*) to the extent of the location of the *bindu*, he emerges...

Having meditated upon the union of Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara, one should place [the mantra] *oṃ hāṃ haṃ hām ātmane namaḥ* within the womb-channel (*garbhanāḍī*) of Vāgīśvarī using the middle channel and the *utpavamudrā*. Then, having performed the meditation on the nine-fold union (*navanāga-dhyāna*) by uniting the Self (*ātman*) with all the birth-places (*sarvayoni*) through the single channel, one should worship it with the root-mantra (*mūla*), offer three oblations (*āhutitraya*), and pray: "O Blessed One, please grant that this Self may achieve union with all the birth-places through the single channel."

Having petitioned [the Lord] with three oblations (*āhuti*) using the *mūla-mantra* for the sake of the ripening of the body within all wombs (*sarvayoni*), saying, "O Lord, may this self attain the ripening of the embryo within all wombs at one and the same time"; and thereafter, having petitioned for the sake of birth (*janman*) with three oblations using the *mūla-mantra*, saying, "O Lord, please grant birth to this self within all embryos."

For the sake of authority, having meditated upon the entire body as being pure and growing simultaneously, one offers three oblations through the *mūlamantra*. Having petitioned the Lord, saying, "May you grant simultaneous growth to this self within all bodies," one proceeds for the purpose of the journey (*bhoga*) with the Śaiva *vijñāna*...

Having meditated upon the accumulated (*sañcita*) and prospective (*āgāmī*) karmas as being unified within a single locus, one offers three oblations (*āhuti*) into the *mūlādhāra*. Then, having petitioned the Lord, saying, "May these accumulated and prospective karmas of this self be unified for the sake of attaining wisdom (*vijñāna*)," [the Lord] grants the experience of all matrices and bodies simultaneously.

Having performed meditation on *karmārjana*, and having offered three oblations (*āhutis*) with the *mūla-mantra*, one should pray: "O Blessed One, please grant various kinds of enjoyment to this self. Having thus petitioned, one should then meditate upon the enjoyment consisting of all forms of suffering, which exists through the accumulated and karmic latent impressions (*saṃcitakarmavāsanā*) that manifest in various forms across space, time, body, and objects.

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra, he petitions the Lord: "May You bring this self to the ripening of its experience (*bhoga*) within all womb-born bodies. Then, meditating upon the intense flow of supreme love for the objects of enjoyment (*bhogyāṅga*), he offers three oblations with the root mantra and petitions the Lord: "May You grant this self the intense flow of supreme love for the objects of enjoyment."

Having offered three oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the purification of the commencement of the flow of Mahāmāyā, and having petitioned, "O Blessed One, please grant the purification of the commencement of the flow of Mahāmāyākārya for this self," one should offer three oblations with the heart-mantra so that the karmas which are the cause of departure may be consumed and rendered incapable of returning to life. Thereafter, one should offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra for the sake of the purification of birth, lifespan, enjoyment, limbs, saṃskāras, and so forth.

Having petitioned the Lord, "May You grant purification for this Self regarding all karmas," and having meditated upon the Self as being separated from Mahāmāyā-śakti so that there is no further wandering [in saṃsāra], one should offer three oblations with the Mūla-mantra. Then, meditating on the function of the impurity (*mala*) consisting of the non-appropriation of one's own nature (*svarūpānavadhāraṇa-mala*), which is attachment to the objects of agency (*bhoktṛtva-viṣaya*), for the purpose of the concealment of *prakṛti*...

In the *Mūlatantra* along with the *Pāśupatāstra*, it is said: "Oṃ ślīṃ paśu haṃ śivāya svāhā. Having offered ten oblations (*āhuti*) with this mantra, one should perform the meditation on the dissolution of the *adhikāra-mala* (the impurity of office). Then, having offered three oblations with the root mantra, one should meditate that the *nāśa* (destruction) has been directly produced, as if the pure rites (*śuddha-karma*) had been performed. Then, having offered three oblations with the root mantra, [one should offer] to the Lord for this self, regarding the *mahāmāyā-śvabhya* (the great illusion of the void).

Having requested that the three impurities (*mala*) consisting of the nature of karma (*karmasvarūpa*) be removed, one should offer three oblations (*āhuti*) with the *Mūla-mantra*. Then, having consecrated the *Kartarī* [knife] sevenfold with the *Astra-mantra*, one should purify it within the expanse of the impurity of the *Śāntyatīta-kalā* by means of the mantra-sound: *oṃ hāṃ śāntyatītakalā... huṃ phaṭ*. Afterward, for the purpose of removing the bonds (*pandha*), [one should act] with the *Atiśāntikalā*...

Having poured [the oblation] into the *sruc* filled with clarified butter (*ājya*) by means of the *astra-mantra*, and having performed the offering ending with "svāhā" by means of the *sahitā-mantra*... thereafter, having offered three oblations (*āhutis*) with the *astra-mantra*, one who reduces the rite to ashes should petition the Lord, saying, "May the Lord grant this soul the state of being beyond the power of *śānti*," for the purpose of removing the bonds of that [power]. (l. 2)

Having offered three oblations with the Astra-mantra while pronouncing "Hum Phaṭ," and having offered seven oblations with the Astra-mantra for the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should contemplate that all [the disciple's] bodies have been rendered non-existent, leaving only consciousness as a single form. Then, in the case of *nirbīja-dīkṣā*, for the purpose of purifying the bonds of the rules of conduct (*samayācāra-pāśa*), [one offers]: *oṃ hāṃ samayācārapāśāya*.

Having performed the invocation (*āvāhana*) and worship of the *samayārthapaśus* with the mantra "Salutation to the Gaṇas," one should offer three *sannidhānāhuti*s ending with "svāhā" according to the [respective] mantras. Then, having offered one hundred and eight oblations (*āhuti*) according to the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*), and five *pūrṇāhuti*s, one should petition: "O Blessed One, please grant this self the purification of the conduct of the *samaya*. Thereafter, having performed the invocation of Sadāśiva according to the root-mantra, [one recites]: "This is the power released by Śiva’s hand, born from the white Bhava."

Having petitioned, "I have now accomplished my purpose; you should not [remain] out of compassion," he subsequently performs the invocation (*āvāhana*) of Sadāśiva by means of the *mūla-mantra*. Then, meditating upon the Self as being situated at the tip of the pure principle (*śuddhatattva*), completely free from the influence of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*, and utterly stainless, he offers three oblations (*āhuti*) with the *mūla-mantra* into the fire for the sake of its extraction, saying: "O Lord, this Self..."

Having petitioned that [the deity] should take [the soul] forth even from the power of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*, one should take the self (*ātman*) forth from the fire by means of the fourfold *ātma-mantra* (p. 54a, l. 1). Then, having brought the self into one's own heart during the autumn season—when it resembles the orb of the moon—one should join it to the disciple's *sūtra-deha* (subtle body) by means of the *reca-ka* breath and the *utpatti-mudrā*. Having performed worship for the sake of nourishment (*āpyāyana*), [one should proceed].

Having sprinkled drops of *arghya* water upon the head of the disciple with the *mūla-mantra* accompanied by the syllable *vauṣaṭ*, and having offered three oblations (*āhuti*) with the *mūla-mantra* for the purpose of stabilization (*sthirīkaraṇa*), one should thereafter worship Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara. Having offered three oblations with their respective mantras, [one recites]: "O parents, you who sacrifice for the initiation (*dīkṣā*) of the disciple, show compassion; come here and nourish him with your own breast. The meaning of this is as follows in the context of the *Dīkṣitayāga*.

Because the invocation (*āvāhana*) and the heating (*uttāpana*) have been performed for a long time, they have become exceedingly radiant. Having offered these four [oblations], one should petition: "May you arise and remain firmly established in your own stations. Having given the *parāṅmukhārghya* to these [deities] and having performed the *udvāsana*, one should offer the final oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) with the root mantra ending in *vaṣaṭ*. This is the purification of the *śāntyatīta-kalā*.

Afterwards, reciting "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the Śāntyātīta-kalā and Śakti," one purifies the Śāntyātīta-kalā which has been purified. Then, having joined it with Tirodhāna-bhāṣyā, who is of the nature of the Purifier (Śodhikā-rūpā), one subsequently performs the salutation to the Ātma-tattva, which is pervasive (vyāpaka), by reciting "Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the Ātma-tattva" (as found in Śikha-śeṣam, p. 54b, f. 50a, l. 1). Having worshipped it, for the sake of the purification of the constituent parts of the ritual (kriyā-aṅga-śuddhi), one should utter the Mūla-mantra nine times.

Having performed one hundred and eight oblations and having offered worship with the mantra “Oṃ Hauṃ, obeisance to the Vidyā-tattva,” which pervades as far as the Śiva-tattva, for the sake of the purification of the entire mantra, one should perform one hundred and eight oblations with the root mantra recited in a low voice (*upāṃśu*). Then, having offered worship with the mantra “Oṃ Hauṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-tattva,” which pervades as far as the Śakti-tattva, [one should offer oblations] with the mantra recited mentally (*mānasa*).

Having offered one hundred and eight oblations with the *mūla-mantra* for the sake of the purity of the *dhyāna-vairāgya-śakti*, and thereafter having offered one hundred and eight oblations with the *mūla-mantra* for the sake of the cessation of the concealment (*tirodhāna*) of the *tirodhāna-śakti*, he should then meditate upon the *Śakti* who pervades all paths (*adhvans*), abiding as distinct from them; at the conclusion of that meditation, he should meditate upon the consciousness (*caitanya*) of the disciple, which has the luster of a pure crystal gem.

The Sevenfold Method... with the stalk of *kardara* consecrated by the mantra *oṃ hūṃ vi? śikhāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ*, (l. 8) for one desiring liberation (*mukti-kāmanā*) above twelve finger-breadths, and for one desiring liberation below eight finger-breadths, having cut the tuft (*śikhā*), [the hair] together with the oil-presser is placed within cow dung... (p. 55a, l. 1).

Having placed the *śikhā* into the *sruc* ladle filled with clarified butter (*ājya*), one should perform the *homa* while reciting "oṃ hūṃ śikhāyai haḥ huṃ phaṭ" and burn it. Then, performing three oblations (*āhutis*) with the *Śivāstra-mantra*, one should reduce it to ashes.

Thereafter, having brought forth another person, having caused the disciple to perform his ablutions, and having cleansed the *sruk*, *sruva*, and *kartarī* [ladles] with the four [mantras], he himself performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) and the purification of the breath (*prāṇāyāma*). Having entered within the pavilion, performed the ritual placement of mantras (*nyāsa*), and worshipped Śiva... [he said: "If this [act] which has been performed for the sake of purifying the impurity of the head-portion of the soul that has entered the temple of Your Majesty, may it lead [him] to the state of Śiva alone."

Having requested, "May Your Honor be pleased to grant your grace," and having had [the preparations] made, he went to the serpent-pit (nāgakuṇḍa) together with the arghya vessel; then, having summoned the disciple and performed the purification of the *sruc* and *sruva* ladles, he kindled the fire for the purpose of performing the *yojanā*, sprinkled the disciple, performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), established the connection of the channels (*nāḍīsaṃtāna*), and offered three oblations (*āhutitraya*) with the root-mantra in order to bring about its presence (*sannidhāna*).

Having performed the oblation (*homa*) with the *saṃhitā* mantras one by one, he speaks for the purpose of manifesting the nature of Śiva (*śivatvavyakti*) in the disciple: (p. 55b, f. 51a, l. 1) having worshipped Śiva with the root-mantra (*mūla*) one by one, and having petitioned [Him] that the manifestation of the nature of Śiva may be granted, subsequently, for the sake of effecting the assumption (*ādāna*) within that very state of Śiva-nature, the desire (*icchā*) existing therein...

For the purpose of [the ritual] becoming manifest, having offered the *dīpana-āhuti* with the *mūla-mantra*, the preceptor shall unite the disciple within Śiva. Afterwards, the preceptor, meditating upon the sacrificial pavilion (*yāgamaṇḍapa*) as the reality of Pure Knowledge (*śuddhavidyātattva*), [offers] the *vāmanātha-kalās* into the fire of the body by means of the *vyāpinīmudrā*.

Having performed meditation upon the Lord of the Nagas—who possesses both external weapons such as the *mudrānakhas* (claw-weapons) and internal weapons—and having sprinkled the disciples with the Astra-mantra, "Oṃ haḥ huṃ phaṭ," while joined with flowers, one should strike them at the region of the heart with the *nārācamudrā*. Then, entering their bodies with one's own *recaka* breath accompanied by the sound "Huṃ," one recites again: "Oṃ hāṃ haṃ hāṃ huṃ phaṭ. Oṃ.

Having received [the offering] with the four *samudrā* mantras beginning with *hāṃ haṃ hāṃ svāhā*, and having taken it up to the extent of the twelve [fingers], one should meditate upon the Self as being in the form of a drop (*bindu*). Then, having received [it] with the four *saṃhāramudrā* mantras beginning with *ā*, and having brought it into the heart, one should consolidate it, bring it to a state of oneness, and [offer] the clarified butter (*ājya*) into the *sruk* with the four [mantras].

Having performed the *sannidhi-mudrā* upon the *sruc*—which has been placed face down and holds a flower at its tip—one should, with hands facing upward, place the base of the *sruc* at the navel; then, having sequentially performed the *nyāsa* of Nivṛtti and the others upon the five limbs, the joints, the knots, the channels, the sacrificial altar, and the mouth, one should [prepare] the stream of clarified butter (*ājya-dhārā*).

Having performed *tyāga-dhyāna* (meditation on renunciation), one should perform *ananya-nātha-dhyāna* (meditation on the Lord who pervades all states) upon the deity residing within the *śrūka*. Remaining as a firm Siddha-nātha (*sthirasiddhanāga*) for the sake of purification (*śodhya*), and being possessed of equal vision (*samadṛṣṭimān*), if [the breath] is joined one with another and placed outside, the Lord of the Body (*vapuṣpati*) performs *pūraka-kumbhaka* (inhalation and retention). Having made the breath (*prāṇa*) and the mind (*manas*) of Śiva into a single unity, [one proceeds] through the *suṣumnā*...

Having performed meditation on the flow of sound (*nādapravāha*), and having performed meditation so as to purify the consciousness of the disciple, the Guru, by means of the method of consecration (*gurupratiṣṭhāprakāra*), should utter the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) and, perceiving the heart, the palate, and the *brahmarandhra*, [visualize] the causal deities beginning with Brahmā situated within the syllables.

Having united [the self] with Śiva—who resides within the *dvādaśānta* in the heart, whose nature is supreme bliss (*paramānanda-svarūpa*), who is beyond the mind (*manātīta*), free from all taints (*pāpaśūnya*), and the source of all other qualities—he remains united. Then, for the sake of his continued stability, he offers the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*). Afterwards, standing behind the *sruc* ladle... [performing the ritual action]... while looking toward the *kalaśas*, he pours clarified butter (*ājya*) through the mouth of the *praśāntanāla* [tube]... *oṃ hāṃ ātman sarva...*

Svāhā! Oṃ him! O Self, be completely satisfied; svāhā! Oṃ hlām! O Self, be awakened; svāhā! Oṃ hyaiṃ... be self-dependent; svāhā! Oṃ ham! O Self, be one whose power is unimpaired; svāhā! Oṃ haḥ! O Self, be one of infinite power; svāhā! Thus, by these [mantras], he brings forth the qualities.

Thereafter, having gazed with divine vision upon the Self—which possesses great splendor like the orb of the sun—and having drawn it back with the *saṃhāramudrā*, he brings it into his own heart. Then, by means of the *utpattimudrā* accompanied by the *reśaka* breath, he places [the Self] within the heart of the disciple for the purpose of purifying the fruits of *prārabdha-karma*. Subsequently, by means of the intensely powerful mantric energies... [the awakening... (Note: The ellipsis indicates the continuation of the ritual process involving the dissolution or awakening of the disciple's consciousness.)

Having sprinkled a drop of *arghya* water, which is like nectar (*amṛta*), upon the head of the disciple who is facing away from the *bhogakūṭa*, and having thereafter paid obeisance to the Lord of the Maṇḍala and the others, one should then place a maṇḍala to the right of Śiva and, seating the disciple there to his own left, [recite]: "This water of grace, which has taken form and is my power (*māmakī*)... [de... (Note: The final portion of the text appears to be a fragment of a mantra or verse concerning the initiation or empowerment of the disciple.)

"Therefore, by your grace, may there be for me an uninterrupted performance of the rites of devotion toward that Guru, Bhaktinātha. O Lord, this vow is the cause for the increase of [your] favor. The meaning of this is: "Taking my body as the locus, you alone, O Lord, must show favor to this disciple; therefore, please ensure that devotion arises toward you, toward Śivāgnidra, and toward Gurunidra," he said without ceasing.

Having requested that the daily obligatory rites (*nitya-kriyā*) must be performed and that the fault of ritual omission (*kriyā-lopa*) incurred by failing to do so must be addressed so as not to become an obstacle to liberation (*mokṣa*), he paid obeisance to Śiva. Then, having bestowed a blessing upon the disciple—saying, "May there be well-being for you again"—the Guru [performed] the festival of initiation (*dīkṣā-utsava*) for the pacification of the planets and other influences... remembering the abode of Kalāpagrama.

One should manifest the yoga of Śiva through the complete extraction of the root-mantra (*mūla-mantra*). Having meditated in this manner, one should thereafter worship Śiva, who resides in the station of fire (*agni-sthāna*). For the sake of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should offer one hundred and eight oblations (*āhuti*) with the root-mantra. Then, for the purpose of the food offering (*naivedya*), one should offer three oblations with the root-mantra using sacrificial porridge (*caru*). After giving water for sipping (*ācamana*), betel leaves (*tāmbūla*), and other items, and having offered the eight flowers (*aṣṭapuṣpa*) and prostrated, one should present the *parāṅmukha-arghya* and perform the *pūrṇāhuti*.

Having performed the rite and awakened Śiva residing in the fire, one should subsequently perform the *homa* in the Śivāgni with the *pūrādhyāna* mantras. Then, having offered the *paridhi-viṣṭara* oblations to Brahmā and the others, as well as to Indra and the others, and having provided water for sipping (*ācamana*), one should offer the inner and outer oblations (*antarbali* and *bahirbali*) to Rudra and the others, as well as to Indra and the others, as before. Having given the water for sipping, one should offer the *viparīta-prāṇmukhārghya* to these [deities] beginning with Brahmā.

Having raised [the deity] and joined him within one's own heart, and having subsequently performed *ācamana* and *nyāsa*, one should worship Śiva residing in the maṇḍala with eight flowers (*aṣṭapuṣpa*). Having offered the power of the ritual action (*kriyābala*) that has been performed, and having prostrated, one should offer the *parānmukārghya*. Then, joining [the deity] within Śiva residing in the pitcher (*kumbha*), one should likewise worship Śiva residing in the pitcher, complete the rite, and offer the *astravartanī* along with the *parānmukārghya*.

Having performed the *mūrti-pañji* (the rite of forming the deity’s form), while reciting the *astramantra*, one should join Śiva... to the *iṣṭaliṅga* within the *kumbha-sthāna*. Having offered the eight flowers (*aṣṭapuṣpa*), performed the hymn of praise (*stotra*), circumambulation (*pradakṣiṇa*), and prostrations (*namaskāra*), and having granted the *parāṅmukhārghya* (the water of dismissal), one should request that the *mūrti-pañji* and the fire-oblation (*homa*) be performed. Then, having worshipped Caṇḍeśvara as before, offered the *nirmālya* (remains of the offering), and performed the worship concluding with the recitation (*japānta-māha*), one should [worship] Caṇḍeśvara for the disciple...

He shall teach the rules of conduct (*samayācāra*). One must not abandon Śiva, the Śiva-scripture, the fire of Śiva, the practitioner (*sādhaka*), or the Guru. One should never, under any circumstances, [discard] the remains of offerings (*nirmālya*)... one should avoid giving [such things away], stepping over them, or discarding them. One should also avoid food from a woman in childbirth, as well as flowers and garments [from such sources]. Non-violence (*ahiṃsā*), [truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness]—may these be fulfilled. Absence of anger, service to the Guru, purity, contentment, and straightforwardness—such are the qualities of right conduct (*ācāra*).

(1.6) Although [this teaching] is common to all, it must be protected according to one's ability by means of the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation. (1.7) The meaning of these [verses] is that one must not revile Śiva, the Śaivāgama, the Śivāgnis, the Sādhakas, or the Guru; nor must one step upon their shadows. One must not consume the *nirmālya* (the remains of offerings), nor should one bestow it upon those who have received the Śiva-initiation (*śivadīkṣā*). (1.8) One must not cross over [it], nor [eat] the food of a woman in childbirth (*sūtikānna*), the food of [those dedicated to] Śiva (*śivānna*), or the food of a menstruating woman (*puṣpavatī*)... [of these].
These are the northern gates. (p. 58b, f. 54a, l. 1) Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy... non-anger, service to the teacher, purity of mind, purity of body, [purity of] speech...

Having obtained permission from these [deities] (l. 2), having worshipped according to one's capacity, and having performed the *homa* at the time of the *naivedya*, one should conclude the worship, perform the *mūrtipratiṣṭhā*, and then, having invoked Caṇḍeśvara from the site of the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) and Caṇḍeśvara from the site of the fire (*agni*), one should perform the *homa* in the Śivāgni with the *pūrādhyāna* mantras in their entirety, and thus [perform] the common... (l. 4) ...in this manner, the *samaya*...

After the *pittu* [offering], having offered the remnants of the sacrifice (*yajñaśeṣa*) into the fire for Caṇḍeśvara, and having recited the mantras for the establishment of the fire (*agnisthāpana*), he should unite [the deity] within his own heart; then, having bowed to the fire and performed the consecration (*mūrti*), he should raise the fire, offer the *arghya* facing away from the sacrificial deities, perform the *utthāpana* in reverse order, and having recited the mantras for the establishment of the *arghyapātra*, he should unite it within his own heart; thereafter, [he should address] the disciple.

Having placed [the disciple] within the maṇḍala at his own station, he should perform the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) with the water from the vardhanī vessel and then with the water from the Śivakuṇḍa. Afterwards, having caused the Guru to rise and take his seat upon the pedestal (*pīṭha*) and other seats with pure water, he should worship the disciple as if he were being worshipped himself. Then, according to his capacity, he should offer a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), such as an elephant or other objects, or many villages, a village, or even a field.

One should offer oneself, endowed with all one's possessions, with faith at the lotus-feet of the Guru, having made oneself his servant; the Teacher himself should accept this from him without causing any hardship. According to these verses, he who gives his body, wealth, and life into the hands of the Ācārya, and the Teacher who accepts these without disregarding the welfare of the disciple’s mind—[both are virtuous].

This sequence of initiation (*dīkṣākrama*), as taught by the gurus—such as the illustrious Bhojadeva, Induśiva, and others—for the sake of awakening to the nature of action and existence, has likewise been written by me in this way for easy understanding. While it is being written, may the Supreme Lord—who is the Great Name in the circle of the earth, who is skilled in all [matters] beginning with the causes, who has reached the further shore of the Vedas, who is a wise man who composes works on the meanings of logic, who is foremost among the commentators on the Śaiva doctrine, and who is the excellent teacher for his disciples—be pleased. [Here ends] the procedure for the initiation into liberation (*nirvāṇadīkṣāvidhi*).

Thus ends the procedure for the initiation into liberation (*nirvāṇadīkṣā-vidhi*) in the *Kriyākramadyotikā*, composed by the venerable Aghoraśivācārya, whose other name is Parameśvara. Hariḥ Om. May it be filled with Śiva. May there be auspiciousness. On the fourteenth day of the month of Mīna in the year Parītāpin, on Thursday; written by hand by Kumāra Aruṇācalaguru of Śālaveḍu Agastīśvaragurukkaḷ. [End of page 59b]
